issues.title: [Epic] Data dictionary: two-layer concept model and cross-stage correlation (Gravity-style)
issues.bodyMd:
Follow-on from the deep review of `/guide/data-dictionary` (accuracy fixes landed separately — see the commit "Correct the data dictionary against LOINC, the FSH, and the mappers").

The accuracy pass fixed what was *wrong*. This epic is about what the dictionary cannot currently *express*, and about turning the correlation machinery SPiER already has into something a partner can query.

## The finding behind this epic

**Most of the Gravity-style structure already exists in the IG. The data dictionary just doesn't show any of it, and the parts that exist don't compose.**

`ig/input/fsh/concept-layer.fsh` is explicitly Gravity-modeled and already has the four pieces Gravity uses:

| Gravity mechanism | SPiER equivalent | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Domain (Food Insecurity, Housing…) | `SPiERConceptDomain#suicide-risk` | exists — `Observation.category` only |
| Grouper concept everything rolls into | `spier-suicide-risk-tier` (5 ordered tiers) | exists, bound `required` |
| Instrument→concept translation | 5 `crosswalk-*.fsh` ConceptMaps + StructureMaps | exist, pending clinical sign-off (#77) |
| Provenance back to the instrument | `derivedFrom 1..*`, must-support | exists |

And `ig/input/fsh/risk-episode.fsh` adds the longitudinal spine: `EpisodeOfCare` as anchor, `Flag` as chart banner, `Task.basedOn → EpisodeOfCare` for open safety actions.

**What's missing is the two-axis grid Gravity gets its power from.** Gravity's real trick isn't the domain list — it's that the *same domain code* rides on `.category` of every resource in the chain (Observation → Condition → Goal → ServiceRequest → Procedure), so one query returns the whole story regardless of resource type or originating instrument. SPiER stamps its domain on the concept Observation and nothing else, while a *second*, unrelated axis (`meta.tag` = pathway-stage) rides on everything.

Today there are four correlation mechanisms that don't compose:

1. `meta.tag` = pathway stage — universal, any resource
2. `Observation.category` = concept domain — concept Observations only
3. `Observation.derivedFrom` — instrument → concept, one hop
4. `Task.basedOn` → `EpisodeOfCare` — Stage 7 only

Nothing threads a Stage-1 ASQ, a Stage-3 safety plan, a Stage-6 caring contact and a Stage-7 episode together as **one patient's one risk episode**.

## Visible symptoms in the dictionary today

- LOINC `93374-7` appears as **four separate, unlinked rows** (`suicide-risk-level`, `bssa-disposition`, `pss3-result`, `safet-risk-level`), plus a fifth instance inside `asq-result`. Five rows, one concept, nothing saying they're the same thing.
- The flat `code` / `codeSystem` pair cannot express "code X, valued from value set Y", so whether a row documents `Observation.code` or `Observation.value` depends on who wrote it.
- `FhirResourceType` is a 4-member union (`QuestionnaireResponse | Observation | Condition | CarePlan`), so `EpisodeOfCare`, `Task`, `Flag`, `ServiceRequest`, `Communication`, `Appointment`, `Procedure`, `DocumentReference`, `Consent` and `Encounter` are inexpressible — the exact resources the Stage-8 measure engine reads.
- 14 of 40 catalogued tools have any entry at all. Whole FSH files have none: `crp.fsh`, `lethal-means.fsh`, `follow-up.fsh`, `handoffs.fsh`, `risk-episode.fsh`, `measure-and-share.fsh`, `crisis-resources.fsh`, `suicide-related-conditions.fsh`. The page does not disclose this, so it reads as complete.
- The ConceptMaps already record `relatedto` / `wider` because ASQ genuinely cannot resolve low vs. moderate vs. high. That lossiness is the most important thing a partner consuming the tier layer needs to know, and it is invisible outside FSH comments.

## Children

- [ ] #260 — Two-layer dictionary schema: separate Concepts from per-instrument Bindings
- [ ] #261 — Put the dictionary under check:codings and retire the parallel terminology manifest
- [ ] #262 — Propagate the concept-domain category across the whole resource chain
- [ ] #263 — Make EpisodeOfCare the correlation key for all eight stages
- [ ] #264 — Surface crosswalk fidelity (wider / relatedto) in the dictionary and the UI
- [ ] #265 — CAMS driver Conditions emit vendor systems instead of the canonical SPiER CodeSystem (spun out of the review)

## Sequencing

The first two are a mechanical refactor of `web/` with a gate attached and can start now. The third and fourth are IG changes needing the publisher and the scenario gates. The fifth depends on the crosswalks getting clinical sign-off, which is still open under #77.

## Open questions for the team

- **`http://cams-care.com/driver-type`** is the only vocabulary the demo emits with no SPiER CodeSystem behind it, and the URL is a vendor marketing site, not a terminology server. Mint `spier.org/CodeSystem/cams-driver-type`, reuse the `cams-careplan-section` direct/indirect codes, or drop the classification?
- **How much of the missing 26 tools to document** vs. explicitly mark "not yet modeled". Either way the page needs a coverage statement — silence currently reads as completeness.

Related: #77 (concept layer epic), #220 (fabricated LOINC codes — same blind-spot class).

issues.title: Data dictionary: split DataElement into Concept + Binding, open the resource union
issues.bodyMd:
Part of #259.

## Problem

`web/src/data/catalog/dataElements.ts` models every row as one flat `code` + `codeSystem` + `codeDisplay` triple. That cannot express the thing SPiER actually does most often: **an Observation coded with one concept and *valued* from a different vocabulary.**

The consequences are visible on the live page:

- LOINC `93374-7` occupies four separate rows (`suicide-risk-level`, `bssa-disposition`, `pss3-result`, `safet-risk-level`) with a fifth instance folded into `asq-result`. Same concept, five entries, no linkage.
- Before the accuracy pass, `asq-result` put the *value* system (`asq-screening-result`) in the code column while `bssa-disposition` and `pss3-result` put the *code* (LOINC 93374-7) there and explained the value in prose. Both readings were defensible under the schema, which is the bug.
- The four SBQ-R item rows name an **answer-option** CodeSystem in the System column against `code: 'N/A'`, because the SBQ-R items carry no item code at all. Nothing in the schema distinguishes "code of the item" from "vocabulary of the answer".

`FhirResourceType` is also a closed 4-member union, so `EpisodeOfCare`, `Task`, `Flag`, `ServiceRequest`, `Communication`, `Appointment`, `Procedure`, `DocumentReference`, `Consent` and `Encounter` cannot be documented — which is most of what Stages 5–8 produce and exactly what the Stage-8 measure engine reads.

## Proposal

Split the flat list into **concepts** and **bindings**, mirroring the two-layer model `concept-layer.fsh` already defines:

```ts
interface Concept {
  id: 'suicide-risk-tier'
  domain: 'suicide-risk'                                   // SPiERConceptDomain
  code: { system: 'http://loinc.org', code: '93374-7', display: 'Suicide risk level' }
  valueSet: 'http://spier.org/ValueSet/spier-suicide-risk-tier-vs'
  narrower?: string[]                                      // instrument concepts that roll up
}

interface Binding {                    // one instrument's expression of a concept
  conceptId: 'suicide-risk-tier'
  toolIds: ['TL-001']
  resource: FhirResourceType           // now open to every R4 type SPiER emits
  code: Coding                         // Observation.code — what identifies the resource
  value?: {                            // Observation.value — separate slot, finally
    kind: 'CodeableConcept' | 'integer' | 'boolean' | 'string'
    valueSet?: string
  }
  path: string                         // resource-qualified FHIRPath
  conceptMap?: 'http://spier.org/ConceptMap/ASQDispositionToRiskTier'
  fidelity?: 'equivalent' | 'wider' | 'relatedto'          // see the fidelity task
  provenance?: 'derivedFrom' | 'basedOn' | 'partOf'
}
```

## Why this shape

- `code` and `value` stop competing for one slot — the §6 conflation becomes unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.
- The five `93374-7` rows collapse into one `Concept` with five `Binding`s, which is also what the page should render: one expandable concept, not five sibling rows.
- `conceptMap` and `valueSet` are canonical URLs, so a gate can resolve them against `web/src/data/fhir/` — the same trick `care-plan-profiles.generated.ts` already uses for CarePlan profile URLs. Nothing in the dictionary is checkable today; after this, most of it is.
- Opening `FhirResourceType` is what makes Stages 5–8 documentable at all.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Concept` / `Binding` types replace `DataElement`; `FhirResourceType` opened to the R4 types SPiER emits
- [ ] All 68 current entries migrated with no loss of information
- [ ] `93374-7` renders as one concept with its five instrument bindings
- [ ] `DataDictionary.tsx` and `PatientJourney.tsx` updated (both consume this data)
- [ ] `primaryStageFor` and `toolsForElement` — currently exported and unused, and `primaryStageFor`'s own comment admits it doesn't sort the way its name implies — either fixed or deleted
- [ ] `npm run verify` green, including `services/cds-hooks` (it imports the web catalog)

issues.title: Put the data dictionary under check:codings and retire the parallel terminology manifest
issues.bodyMd:
Part of #259.

## Problem

`DATA_ELEMENTS` has **no gate whatsoever**. Nothing in `web/scripts/` reads it, there are no tests, and — the important part — `npm run check:codings` cannot see it despite scanning `web/src`.

`check-codings.mjs` finds a terminology-system URL literal, walks out to the enclosing object, and then requires `field(obj, 'system') === system` before it will extract anything (`web/scripts/check-codings.mjs:245`). The dictionary writes `codeSystem: 'LOINC'` — a friendly name, not a URL, and not in a field called `system`. So zero of its rows have ever been validated.

That is issue #220's blind spot reproduced in the artifact an implementer is most likely to read as "the codes to use". The accuracy pass found 15 of 16 LOINC displays drifted, including `93267-3` labelled with a question when the code is a finding — the same shape as the `81344-4` problem in #220.

Meanwhile `docs/terminology-manifest.json` is a **second, parallel inventory** with a different shape: it uses `system` as a URL (so `check:codings` does see it) but carries no `display` at all, so it validates code existence only. Neither inventory is derived from the other, and the manifest lists codes the dictionary has never mentioned — SNOMED `225337009` appears against every tool there and appeared in no dictionary row until the accuracy pass.

## Proposal

Fold the manifest into the dictionary as the single inventory, in a shape `check:codings` already understands:

- `Coding` objects with `system` as a **URL** (`http://loinc.org`, not `'LOINC'`), plus `code` and `display`
- render the friendly name in the UI from the URL, not the other way round
- delete `docs/terminology-manifest.json` once its contents are represented, and update the `SCAN` entry in `check-codings.mjs`

Because the extractor scans object literals rather than matching a fixed field order, this needs **no change to `check-codings.mjs`'s extraction logic** — only the `SCAN` floors.

## Watch the floors

`SCAN`'s `minCodings` floors assert liveness, not completeness, at roughly half the real count — and per CLAUDE.md, #232 is the cautionary tale: #43 doubled the manifest's SNOMED inventory while its floor sat at 5, quietly dropping to a quarter of the real count with nothing going red. Moving the manifest's codes into `web/src` moves them between `SCAN` entries, so **both** entries' floors need re-deriving in the same PR, not just the destination's.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Dictionary codings use system URLs and are extracted by `check:codings`
- [ ] `docs/terminology-manifest.json` removed or reduced to a pointer
- [ ] `SCAN` floors re-derived for **both** affected entries, with the live counts recorded in the PR
- [ ] Deliberately break a display locally and confirm the nightly **fails** — per CLAUDE.md, a green gate nobody has seen go red is not evidence of anything
- [ ] `docs/scheduled-checks-triage.md` updated if the failure signature changes

issues.title: Propagate the concept-domain category across the whole resource chain (Gravity pattern)
issues.bodyMd:
Part of #259. **This is the actual Gravity move.**

## Problem

Gravity's power doesn't come from having a domain list. It comes from the *same domain code* riding on `.category` of **every resource in the chain** — Observation → Condition → Goal → ServiceRequest → Procedure — so one query returns the complete story for a social risk regardless of resource type or which instrument produced it.

SPiER defines the domain (`SPiERConceptDomain#suicide-risk`, `concept-layer.fsh`) and then applies it in exactly one place: the harmonized concept Observation, as a sliced `category[suicideRisk] 1..1`.

So today:

```
GET /Observation?category=http://spier.org/CodeSystem/spier-concept-domain|suicide-risk
```

returns concept Observations and nothing else. Not the safety-plan CarePlan, not the CAMS driver Conditions, not the referral, not the caring contact, not the episode.

## Proposal

Carry `SPiERConceptDomain#suicide-risk` in `category` on every resource in the suicide-safer-care chain, **alongside** whatever clinical category or pathway-stage tag is already there:

| Resource | Where | Profiles affected |
|---|---|---|
| `Condition` | `Condition.category` | `spier-cams-suicide-driver`, `suicide-related-conditions.fsh` |
| `CarePlan` | `CarePlan.category` | Stanley-Brown, CRP, CAMS stabilization, CAMS therapeutic |
| `ServiceRequest` | `ServiceRequest.category` | referral / rapid-referral profiles |
| `Procedure` | `Procedure.category` | means-safety counseling |
| `Communication` | `Communication.category` | caring contacts, crisis resources |
| `Task` | `Task.code` or an extension (R4 `Task` has no `category`) | Stage-7 safety tasks |
| `EpisodeOfCare` | `EpisodeOfCare.type` (already `suicide-safer-care`) — add the domain coding | `spier-suicide-risk-episode` |
| `Appointment` / `DocumentReference` / `Consent` | resource-appropriate slot | Stages 5–6 |

Then the one query above returns the whole record across every resource type, from any FHIR server, with **no SPiER-specific knowledge required** — which is the interoperability claim the adoption guide is making.

## Design notes

- Follow the existing slicing idiom rather than inventing one: `concept-layer.fsh` already uses a pattern-discriminated, `#open` slice (US Core vitals style) precisely so standard categories like `survey` coexist without the validator warnings a blanket extensible binding raises. Reuse that shape everywhere.
- `Task` has no `category` in R4. Decide between `Task.code` (already carrying the safety-task vocabulary) and a domain extension — the latter is probably cleaner since `Task.code` is load-bearing for `risk-episode.fsh`.
- This is **additive**. Nothing loses its existing category, and the pathway-stage `meta.tag` stays exactly as it is. The two axes are orthogonal on purpose: stage answers "where in the pathway", domain answers "what is this about".

## Gates

Per CLAUDE.md, this touches slicing, which `check:scenarios` explicitly does **not** check — the offline half misses slices, cardinality counts and invariants. So:

- [ ] `npx fsh-sushi .` clean
- [ ] `node scripts/validate-fhir.mjs` clean (this is the half that sees slicing)
- [ ] `ig-publish.yml` dispatched and green — `gh workflow run ig-publish.yml`
- [ ] `npm run check:scenarios` — the scenario fixtures need the new category too, or the profile `min` check will fail
- [ ] `npm run copy-fhir -- --force` then `npm run verify`

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every SPiER profile in the chain carries the suicide-risk domain category
- [ ] Scenario fixtures in `web/src/data/population/scenarios/` updated
- [ ] A single `?category=…|suicide-risk` query across resource types is documented in the IG and demonstrated in the adoption guide

issues.title: Make EpisodeOfCare the correlation key for all eight stages, not just Stage 7
issues.bodyMd:
Part of #259. Highest-leverage item in the epic.

## Problem

`risk-episode.fsh` establishes `EpisodeOfCare` as "the anchor resource for Stage 7" and hangs every Stage-7 `Task` off it via `Task.basedOn`. Stages 1–6 have no such link. There is no way to ask "show me everything that happened in this patient's risk episode".

The cost is visible in `web/src/lib/patientPathway.ts`, which reassembles the journey by **inference** through a four-step fallback chain (`stageForArtifact`):

1. `meta.tag` against the pathway-stage CodeSystem
2. `category.coding` against the same system
3. QuestionnaireResponse → its Questionnaire → its tool → its stage
4. **CarePlan id regex** — `/stanley-brown/i`, `/cams-stabilization/i`, `/crisis-response-plan/i`, `/cams-therapeutic/i`

Step 4 is a heuristic standing in for a missing link, and it only resolves *stage*, never *which episode*. Two risk episodes six months apart are indistinguishable to any consumer.

## Proposal

Every artifact produced along the pathway references its episode:

| Resource | Link |
|---|---|
| `Observation` | `Observation.partOf` → `EpisodeOfCare` |
| `QuestionnaireResponse` | `QuestionnaireResponse.encounter` + episode extension (R4 QR has no `partOf`) |
| `CarePlan` | `CarePlan.addresses` / extension → `EpisodeOfCare` |
| `ServiceRequest` | `ServiceRequest.basedOn` |
| `Communication` | `Communication.partOf` |
| `Task` | `Task.basedOn` — **already done** |
| `Appointment` | `Appointment.basedOn` |
| `Procedure` | `Procedure.partOf` |

Then the whole journey is one query:

```
GET /EpisodeOfCare/{id}?_revinclude=*
```

`risk-episode.fsh` already documents the registry query in this idiom (`EpisodeOfCare?type=suicide-safer-care&status=active&_revinclude=Task:based-on`); this generalizes it from one resource type to all of them.

## Design notes

- R4 has no universal "episode" pointer, so this is per-resource and a couple of slots need an extension. Worth defining **one** `spier-episode-reference` extension and applying it wherever a native element doesn't exist, rather than a different shape per resource.
- The demo mappers currently emit standalone resources with no episode context, so this needs a runtime story too — probably "the recorder stamps the active episode", which means the episode has to exist before Stage 1 completes. That ordering question is the real design work here and should be settled before any FSH is written.
- Once this lands, `stageForArtifact`'s step-4 CarePlan id regex can go — and `patientPathway.ts` gets a lot smaller.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Episode-reference mechanism decided (native element vs. extension, per resource) and written down
- [ ] Profiles updated; `validate-fhir.mjs` and `ig-publish.yml` green
- [ ] Recorders stamp the active episode; scenario fixtures carry it
- [ ] `patientPathway.ts` resolves episode membership by reference, with the id-regex fallback removed or demoted to legacy-only
- [ ] The `_revinclude` journey query documented in the IG

issues.title: Surface crosswalk fidelity (wider / relatedto) and draft status in the data dictionary
issues.bodyMd:
Part of #259. Depends on the crosswalks getting clinical sign-off (#77).

## Problem

The per-instrument ConceptMaps in `ig/input/fsh/crosswalk-*.fsh` already record equivalence conservatively, and the reason is clinical, not bureaucratic. From `crosswalk-asq.fsh`:

> Equivalence is marked conservatively (`relatedto`) for the positive tiers because a single ASQ disposition does not resolve finer severity.

And `concept-layer.fsh` states the governing rule:

> Lower-fidelity instruments map to the widest defensible tier (recorded as a 'wider' equivalence in the per-instrument ConceptMap); the layer never fabricates precision the instrument cannot support.

**None of that reaches a consumer.** The data dictionary shows `93374-7 → Suicide risk level` for ASQ, PSS-3, BSSA, SAFE-T and C-SSRS with nothing distinguishing them. A partner reading the page cannot tell that a `moderate` tier from SAFE-T is a clinician's direct judgment while a `moderate` from ASQ is a lossy widening of a three-way disposition that cannot resolve low from moderate from high.

That asymmetry is the single most important thing to know before acting on the tier layer, and today it lives only in FSH comments.

Note the one genuine exception, which the dictionary should also make visible: **SAFE-T binds directly to `spier-suicide-risk-tier` with no per-instrument crosswalk at all** (`safet-risk-level`) — it lands on the concept layer natively. That is a real fidelity difference, not a documentation gap.

## Proposal

1. Carry `fidelity` on each `Binding` (see the schema task), read from the ConceptMap's `element.target.equivalence` rather than hand-typed — `check-concept-crosswalk.mjs` already parses these maps, so the value can be derived.
2. Render it: a `wider` / `relatedto` binding gets a visible marker and a one-line explanation of what precision is *not* available.
3. State the direct-binding case explicitly where it applies (SAFE-T).
4. Keep the `!! PENDING CLINICAL SIGN-OFF !!` status visible in the UI while it is true. Every crosswalk row is a clinical-equivalence claim, and the adoption guide should not present proposed mappings as settled ones — this is the same failure mode as the licensing claims in #127 and the `careplan-us-profile` row the accuracy pass deleted.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `fidelity` derived from ConceptMap `equivalence`, not hand-maintained
- [ ] Lossy bindings visually distinguished in the dictionary, with the lost precision named
- [ ] Draft / pending-sign-off status surfaced rather than implied
- [ ] `npm run check:crosswalk` extended to fail if a binding's declared fidelity disagrees with its ConceptMap

issues.title: CAMS driver Conditions emit vendor cams-care.com systems instead of the canonical SPiER CodeSystem
issues.bodyMd:
Found during the data-dictionary review (#259). Small, self-contained, and a real IG-vs-runtime divergence.

## The divergence

`web/src/lib/observationMappers/camsSectionB.ts` emits CAMS driver Conditions with:

```ts
category: [
  { coding: [{ system: 'http://cams-care.com/driver-category', code: 'suicide-driver', display: 'Suicide Driver' }] },
  ...(driverType ? [{ coding: [{ system: 'http://cams-care.com/driver-type', code: driverType.code, display: driverType.display }] }] : []),
]
```

But `ig/input/fsh/cams.fsh:41` is explicit that the canonical system is SPiER-local:

> **Description:** "Marker category used on Condition resources that represent CAMS-identified suicide drivers. **Mirrors** `http://cams-care.com/driver-category` for SPiER artifacts that need to surface drivers on the FHIR problem list."

and `SPiERCAMSSuicideDriver` (`cams.fsh:160`) identifies drivers by `http://spier.org/CodeSystem/cams-driver-category#suicide-driver`.

Per CLAUDE.md, `ig/` is canonical for CodeSystems. The runtime is emitting a vendor marketing-site URL that is not a resolvable terminology server, and the published IG examples and the demo output disagree.

The data dictionary has been corrected to follow the IG (with a note pointing here); `tool-ui-metadata.ts:205-206` and `camsSectionB.test.ts:16` carry the same vendor URLs and would need updating together.

## Second, harder half: `driver-type`

`http://cams-care.com/driver-type` (`direct` / `indirect`) has **no SPiER CodeSystem at all** — it is the only vocabulary the demo emits with nothing canonical behind it. `cams.fsh` expresses the same direct/indirect distinction only as *CarePlan section* codes (`cams-careplan-section#direct-drivers` / `#indirect-drivers`), which are a different modelling slot and not reusable as a `Condition.category`.

Three options, needs a decision:

1. **Mint `spier.org/CodeSystem/cams-driver-type`** with `#direct` / `#indirect` — most consistent with how every other CAMS vocabulary is handled, and cheap.
2. **Reuse the section codes** — avoids a new CodeSystem, but overloads a CarePlan-section vocabulary onto Condition.category, which is the kind of shortcut `safety-plan-section.fsh` deliberately avoided when it kept CAMS and Stanley-Brown sections separate.
3. **Drop the classification from `Condition.category`** and keep direct/indirect only where CAMS actually structures it (the Therapeutic Worksheet sections).

## Acceptance

- [ ] `camsSectionB.ts` emits `http://spier.org/CodeSystem/cams-driver-category#suicide-driver`
- [ ] `tool-ui-metadata.ts` and `camsSectionB.test.ts` updated to match
- [ ] `driver-type` decision made and implemented; if a CodeSystem is minted, it lands in `cams.fsh` with a ValueSet and a binding on `SPiERCAMSSuicideDriver`
- [ ] The dictionary's `cams-driver` / `cams-driver-type` notes updated to drop the divergence warning
- [ ] `npm run verify` and `node scripts/validate-fhir.mjs` green

issues.title: Extend the concept-domain tag to Appointment, EpisodeOfCare and Task
issues.bodyMd:
Follow-up from #271, which implemented #262 for the 28 profiles whose resource type has a native `category` element.

These three do not, and each needs a different answer — which is why they were left out rather than guessed at:

| Resource | R4 reality | Candidate slot | Search parameter |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EpisodeOfCare` | no `category`; has `type` 0..* | `type` — already carries `spier-episode-type#suicide-safer-care` | `type` |
| `Appointment` | no `category`; has `serviceCategory` 0..* | `serviceCategory` (example binding) | `service-category` |
| `Task` | no `category`; `Task.code` 0..1 is load-bearing for `risk-episode.fsh` | extension, or a second coding on `code` | **none** without a custom SearchParameter |

## Why this is not just "do the same thing three more times"

The value of the domain tag is that a consumer uses **one parameter value across every type**. These three break that in different ways:

- `EpisodeOfCare` and `Appointment` would need a different parameter *name* (`type`, `service-category`), so a consumer needs to know the exception.
- `Task` has no searchable slot at all. An extension is not queryable without SPiER publishing a SearchParameter and servers supporting it — so tagging Task would create the appearance of coverage with none of the retrievability.

Putting a domain code into those slots without settling that is worse than leaving them out, which is what #271 concluded.

## Options

1. **Tag EpisodeOfCare and Appointment, leave Task to `basedOn`.** Task is already reachable via `GET /EpisodeOfCare/[id]?_revinclude=Task:based-on`, which is arguably the right access path anyway — a Task is not a standalone clinical fact.
2. **Publish a SPiER SearchParameter for a domain extension** and apply it to all three uniformly. Most consistent, most infrastructure, and depends on server support SPiER cannot assume.
3. **Leave all three to the episode**, and make #263 (EpisodeOfCare as correlation key for all eight stages) the retrieval story for anything without a native category.

Option 3 has the appeal of not fighting R4 — but it depends on #263 landing first.

## Already documented

`ig/input/pagecontent/quick-starts.md` states the gap and gives the working retrieval path for each of the three, so the IG does not currently overstate coverage. Whatever is decided here should update that table.

Refs #259, #262, #263.

issues.title: Gate the shape of SUSHI warnings, so the 33rd one is not invisible
issues.bodyMd:
## What changed

#271 (merged as 7dccc25) sliced `.category` on 28 profiles to carry
`spier-concept-domain#suicide-risk`. The slicing is `#open` by design, so
example Instances that set a standard category by numeric index
(`* category[+] = …#survey`) now each emit an advisory warning:

```
warn  Sliced element Observation.category is being accessed via numeric index. Use slice names in rule paths when possible.
```

The repo went from `0 Errors  0 Warnings` to `0 Errors  32 Warnings`. All 32 are
that one advisory, across `Observation`, `CarePlan`, `Communication` and
`Condition`.

## Why they were not silenced

Deliberate, and documented at length in `ig/input/fsh/concept-layer.fsh`. The
only way to silence them is to declare a named slice for every standard category
too — a `survey` slice on each Observation profile, and so on. That constrains
~28 profiles further in order to quiet a linter, and it pins each instance to
one standard category, which several profiles genuinely do not have. That is a
real conformance cost paid for cosmetics. Not doing it was the right call.

**This issue is not a proposal to revisit that.** Leave the warnings.

## The actual gap

Until #271, "SUSHI is quiet" was a usable signal. It no longer is — the 33rd
warning, the real one, now arrives invisible in a field of 32 expected ones. The
in-source comment tells a *human reader* not to fix them. Nothing tells CI.

`ig.yml`'s sushi job is a bare `sushi .` with no assertion on warnings at all.
This is the same class of blind spot as the `check:codings` floors and the
CQL `Translating CQL source` log assertion: the gate is green, and green means
nothing until something asserts *what* green consists of.

## Proposed fix

Gate the warning **shape**, not the count. In the `Compile FSH` step, capture
SUSHI's output and fail if any warning line does not match the known advisory:

```
Sliced element <Type>.category is being accessed via numeric index.
```

Shape rather than an exact number, deliberately: pinning `32` would churn on
every new example Instance and would train people to bump the number without
reading it — the failure mode #232 already demonstrated with a stale floor.

### Traps for whoever picks this up

- **`npm install -g fsh-sushi` emits its own warnings** in the same job
  (`npm warn deprecated inflight@1.0.6`, `glob@7.2.3`, `rimraf@2.6.3`). A naive
  `grep -i warn` over the step's output false-positives on all three. Parse
  SUSHI's own `warn  ` output, or scope the capture to the compile command.
- **`sushi` exits 0 with warnings**, so the check has to read output, not status.
- The summary line is parseable if preferred to per-line matching:
  `| You seem to be casting about.          0 Errors     32 Warnings |`
  — but note SUSHI's summary banner text is randomized per run, so match on the
  `N Errors` / `N Warnings` fields, not the sentence.
- **Prove it can fail before trusting it.** Plant a warning that is not the
  category advisory — an unresolved reference in a draft profile will do — and
  confirm the job goes red. A gate nobody has watched fail is not evidence of
  anything (see `docs/scheduled-checks-triage.md` and the standing repo rule).

## Scope

`.github/workflows/ig.yml` only. No FSH changes. Small, self-contained, no
dependency on the rest of the #262 epic.

issues.title: [Epic] Suicide Care Dashboard: a CoCM registry spec, and the five gaps it exposes
issues.bodyMd:
Tracking epic for the *Suicide Care Dashboard* deck authored by the SPiER project lead (received 2026-08-11) — a 13-slide specification for a suicide-care patient registry / dashboard.

**Requirements source:** `docs/reference/suicide-care-dashboard-spec.md`
**Implementation analysis:** `docs/plans/suicide-care-dashboard.md`

## The framing finding

**The deck specifies a Collaborative Care Model (CoCM) registry.** It never says so, but three of twelve panels and four of nine filters are scoped by a specific role triad — Primary Care Provider, Behavioral Health Care Manager, Psychiatric Consultant — which is the AIMS Center / IMPACT structure. Per panel 6, the consultant **must approve before a patient's risk level is reduced**.

SPiER is currently role-agnostic: there is no `CareTeam`, `PractitionerRole` or `Practitioner` anywhere in `ig/input/fsh/` or the population scenarios.

## The core insight

**The deck is not asking for a new dashboard. It is asking for four more pivots over the query SPiER already computes, plus one role model it does not have.**

`deriveRegistryRow` already returns per-patient risk tier, stage, open/overdue task counts, next appointment, no-show and unreached streaks, open referrals and a recommended next step. Panels 1, 2, 5, 7 and 8 are all re-projections of that same row — grouped by tier, by due date, by work type, by severity. The Population view renders exactly one of the available pivots.

So most of the deck is a presentation problem over data that exists, and a small identifiable remainder needs real FHIR modeling.

## The five modeling gaps

| # | Gap | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **No care-team role model** — one grep hit repo-wide, and it is a string literal | panels 6, 7 (role scoping), 4 of 9 filters |
| 2 | **Reassessment interval is a rule nobody encodes** (High 7d / Mod 14d / Low 30d) | panel 5, 1 tile on panel 1, 1 measure on panel 9, 2 alerts on panel 8 |
| 3 | **"Historical Risk" is a fifth tier** — and probably should be a second axis, not an ordinal level | panel 2, 1 tile on panel 1 |
| 4 | **No approval gate on risk step-down** | panel 6, 1 measure on panel 9 |
| 5 | **Outcome measures need resources SPiER does not emit** (`Encounter`; time series) | panel 10 |

## Phases

- [x] **Phase 1 — Population view dashboard zones.** No new FHIR. → #278, merged as #292.
- [x] **Phase 2 — Encode the per-tier reassessment interval.** One small artifact. → #279, merged as #295.
      Its `Risk Reassessment On Time` measure was split out to #296 — pairing consecutive
      assessments against a tier-dependent, PlanDefinition-sourced window is a new class of
      measure logic, not another group.
- [ ] **Phase 3 — Historical-risk axis.** Needs the concept-layer decision (gap 3) and spec questions 5 + 6.
- [ ] **Phase 4 — `CareTeam` / `PractitionerRole` role model.** Unlocks the consultant + care-manager views, the role filters, and the approval gate. Needs spec questions 3 + 4.
- [ ] **Phase 5 — Outcome measures.** `Encounter`, a time-series report shape, and the largest scope in the deck.

Ordered to front-load everything that needs no new FHIR and to defer both gaps that need an answer from the deck's author. Phases 1 and 2 are deliberately sized to be shippable without answering any open question.

## Stage 8's status changes

`docs/plans/stage-8-measure-and-share.md` presented seven process measures as the whole of Stage 8. The deck breaks that doc's core insight in one specific way: *"every measure is a query over artifacts stages 1–7 already produce"* is true of process measures and false of outcome measures. Recorded there as a new **"Update — the deck adds an outcome half"** section. Honest status is now **process half built, outcome half unmodeled**.

## ⚠️ Terminology finding — the deck cites one wrong code

Slide 13 lists suicide-related diagnosis codes as "e.g. R45.851, Z91.82/Z91.5". Verified against ICD-10-CM on 2026-08-11:

| Code | Actual meaning | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `R45.851` | Suicidal ideations | ✅ correct |
| `Z91.5` | Personal history of self-harm | ⚠️ valid subcategory but **non-billable** — needs `Z91.51` or `Z91.52` |
| `Z91.82` | **Personal history of military deployment** | ❌ **wrong code**, not suicide-related |

Intended pair is almost certainly `Z91.51` (personal history of suicidal behavior) and `Z91.52` (personal history of nonsuicidal self-harm).

This is the #220 failure mode exactly: a code that resolves cleanly against the publishing authority while meaning something else, so no validator can catch it. A vendor following slide 13 literally would capture military-deployment history as a suicide-risk field. **No repo change is needed** — SPiER codes problem-list Conditions in SNOMED CT (`ig/input/fsh/suicide-related-conditions.fsh`, with a written rationale and a tx.fhir.org verification record) — but the deck should be corrected before it circulates further.

The deck's ICD-10 ask is not a reason to switch off SNOMED; it is a reason to publish a crosswalk, because sites register in SNOMED and bill in ICD-10.

## Open questions for the deck's author

Eight in total, listed in the spec doc. The four that gate phases:

1. **Panel 4 lists "Safety Plan Completed" and "Stanley Brown Safety Plan Completed" as separate gauges** — what is the first one? (gates phase 1's compliance gauges)
3. **How hard is the consultant approval gate** — reportable expectation, or a real state-transition guard? (gates phase 4's model choice)
4. **Are the panel-5 reassessment intervals and the panel-6 consultant review cadence one schedule or two?** They differ for Low ("every 30 days" vs "monthly"). (gates phase 2's scope)
5. **Is "Historical Risk" a tier or a lifetime-history axis?** (gates phase 3)

Also unanswered and needed by three separate panel items: **the safety-plan review interval**, which the deck never states.

issues.title: Population view: summary strip, tier census, per-patient alerts panel and a view switcher
issues.bodyMd:
Phase 1 of the Suicide Care Dashboard epic. **Needs no new FHIR** — every number below is derivable from data `deriveRegistryRow` already returns, which is why it is first.

Spec: `docs/reference/suicide-care-dashboard-spec.md` (panels 1, 2, 8, 11)
Plan: `docs/plans/suicide-care-dashboard.md` (§ Population view redesign, phase 1)

## The shape

The Population view is currently one table, six columns, two filters. The deck implies **three zones on one page**.

### Zone 1 — Summary strip (panels 1–2)

Compact KPI tiles plus a risk-tier census bar.

**5 of the 9 executive-summary tiles are derivable today:**

| Tile | Source |
|---|---|
| Patients on Suicide Care Pathway | count of rows with `episodeOpen` |
| High / Moderate / Low Risk | `riskCounts` |
| New Positive PHQ-9 Question 9 Today | Observation query over the slice |

The other four are deliberately out of scope here: *Historical Risk* needs gap 3 (phase 3), *C-SSRS Due Today* and *Safety Plans Needing Update* need gap 2 (phase 2), *Psychiatric Consultations Overdue* needs gaps 1/4 (phase 4). **Render them as explicitly unavailable rather than as zero** — a blank "0 overdue" is indistinguishable from "we cannot compute this", and the Stage-8 dashboard already set the precedent of saying which artifact an empty number is waiting on (`measureGaps.ts`, #213).

⚠️ **`riskCounts` is already computed in `PopulationView.tsx` and currently used only to label filter-menu options.** The tier census exists and is thrown away.

### Zone 2 — Alerts panel (panel 8)

Red/yellow severity, **grouped by patient**, each row linking to that chart.

The insight worth building on: `web/src/lib/measureGaps.ts` already computes *which measure a patient failed and why*, keyed by `Measure.id`, and `MeasureDashboard` renders it **per measure**. The deck wants the same information **per patient**. Same engine, transposed — this is not a new rules engine.

Rules in scope for this phase (6 of 8):

- 🔴 High Risk patient not contacted in 7 days
- 🔴 Safety Plan missing
- 🔴 Positive PHQ-9 without C-SSRS
- 🔴 Missing emergency contact
- 🟡 PCP review overdue
- 🟡 Safety Plan due for review — **only if** the review interval question is answered; otherwise defer with the two below

Deferred to phase 2 (need the interval rule): *reassessment due in 48 hours*, and *psychiatric consultation overdue* to phase 4.

### Zone 3 — Caseload table with a view switcher

The deck contains four tables over the same rows (general caseload, reassessment tracker, care-manager queue, consultant queue). **Build one table whose view selector swaps columns, default sort and default filter — not four components.** `DerivedRegistryRow` stays the single source, and four near-duplicate tables never get a chance to drift.

This phase ships the **scaffold plus the existing Caseload view only**. The Reassessment view lands in phase 2; Work queue and Consultant follow later.

### Filters

Add **age** (derivable from `dob` today). Clinic and the three role filters wait for phase 4. Diagnosis and insurance are deliberately skipped — they are the two filters on panel 11 with no stated metric depending on them.

## ⚠️ The design constraint to respect

**The deck's summary is a management artifact; the Population view is a triage artifact.** Ten KPI tiles stacked above a worklist push actual patients below the fold, which is the one thing a triage view must not do.

Recommendation from the plan: keep zone 1 **compact and collapsible on one page** rather than splitting Dashboard / Caseload into two tabs — the deck's own argument is that the census and the worklist are the same query, and two tabs would deny that. This is a recommendation, not a settled decision, and this phase is where it gets tested.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Summary strip renders the 5 derivable tiles; the 4 blocked tiles state what they are waiting on rather than showing 0
- [ ] Tier census bar reads from `riskCounts` (no second count computed)
- [ ] Alerts panel renders 6 rules grouped by patient, reusing `measureGaps.ts` rather than a new rules engine
- [ ] View-switcher scaffold in place with the Caseload view; adding a view is a config change, not a new component
- [ ] Age filter added
- [ ] Zone 1 does not push the first table row below the fold at 1280×800 or on mobile
- [ ] `npm run verify` green in `web/`; stylelint design tokens respected (no raw hex, `var(--…)` for colors/sizes)
- [ ] `npm install && npm run verify` in `services/cds-hooks/` if the catalog or scenarios are touched

## Out of scope

Everything needing new FHIR. Panels 3, 6, 9, 10 and 12 entirely.

---

issues.title: Encode the per-tier reassessment interval, so "next due" is calculated rather than typed
issues.bodyMd:
Phase 2 of the Suicide Care Dashboard epic. **The best value-to-effort ratio in the deck** — one small artifact unlocks items on four separate panels.

Spec: `docs/reference/suicide-care-dashboard-spec.md` (panel 5)
Plan: `docs/plans/suicide-care-dashboard.md` (gap 2)

## The gap

The deck states a per-tier reassessment interval and describes it as **"automatically calculated according to pathway intervals"**:

| Tier | Interval |
|---|---|
| High Risk | Every 7 days |
| Moderate Risk | Every 14 days |
| Low Risk | Every 30 days |
| Historical | As indicated |

**In SPiER today it is not calculated at all.** `Task` due dates are minted by `web/src/lib/riskEpisode.ts` from a caller-supplied `dueDate`, and the only caller is a date input in `web/src/components/SafetyTaskView.tsx:137` that defaults to today. The interval lives in a clinician's head, and nothing in the repo knows that a high-risk patient is due in 7 days.

## What encoding it unlocks

Four things across four panels, which is why this is disproportionately worth doing:

1. **Panel 5** — the Reassessment Tracker's *Next Due* and *Status* columns, and the third view in the phase-1 view switcher
2. **Panel 1** — the *C-SSRS Due Today* tile
3. **Panel 9** — the *Risk Reassessment On Time >90%* measure
4. **Panel 8** — the *reassessment due in 48 hours* alert, and the *High Risk patient not contacted in 7 days* rule gets a real interval behind it instead of a hardcoded 7

## Modeling options

Two candidates, both small:

- **Per-tier `timing` on a reassessment `ActivityDefinition`** — idiomatic, keeps the rule with the activity it governs, and the stage PlanDefinition can reference it
- **A tier→interval `ConceptMap`** — more explicit as data, easier to read from TypeScript, but a slightly odd use of ConceptMap (it maps a code to a duration, not a code to a code)

Recommendation: the ActivityDefinition, unless reading it from the app turns out to be awkward.

Whichever is chosen, the derived due date must be **computed on read, never stored** — the same decision `overdueTaskCount` already makes in `registry.ts`, so it cannot disagree with the clock.

## ⚠️ One thing the deck does not state

**There is no safety-plan review interval anywhere in the deck**, despite three items depending on one: *Safety Plans Needing Update* (panel 1), *Safety Plan due for review* (panel 8), and *review dates* (data element 7).

This is open question 8 for the deck's author: is it the same per-tier cadence as reassessment, a single fixed interval, or event-driven (reviewed whenever the tier changes)? **Do not guess** — a review interval invented here would silently become the reference implementation. Ship the reassessment interval and leave the safety-plan review items blocked until answered.

Related: open question 4 asks whether the panel-5 reassessment intervals and the panel-6 consultant review cadence are one schedule or two — they differ for Low ("every 30 days" vs "monthly"). If they are one schedule, this artifact serves phase 4 too.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The interval table exists as a FHIR artifact in `ig/input/fsh/`, not as a TypeScript constant
- [ ] The app reads it from the generated JSON (the `measures.ts` precedent: wiring is read from generated FHIR, not hand-copied, so changing the FSH changes the behavior)
- [ ] Next-due is computed on read, never persisted
- [ ] Reassessment view added to the phase-1 view switcher: Patient · Tier · Last assessment · Next due · Status
- [ ] *C-SSRS Due Today* tile computes; *reassessment due in 48 hours* alert fires
- [ ] `Risk Reassessment On Time` measure added — needs a `Measure` + group in `measure-and-share.fsh`, CQL in `ig/input/cql/` (the IG Publisher **does** compile it), and a criterion in `measures.ts` or `npm run check:measures` fails
- [ ] A drift guard ties the app's interval reading to the FSH, following the `check:catalog` / `check:measures` pattern
- [ ] **Plant a defect and watch the guard go red before reporting it green** — a gate never seen to fail is not evidence of anything
- [ ] Safety-plan review items remain explicitly blocked, not silently defaulted

## Out of scope

The safety-plan review interval (blocked on question 8). The consultant review cadence (phase 4).
