issues.title: lint:css enforces var() but never checks that the token exists
issues.bodyMd:
## Problem

`lint:css` enforces that colour/size/shadow declarations use a design token, but
**not that the token exists.** The rule is
`scale-unlimited/declaration-strict-value` with:

```json
"ignoreValues": ["transparent", "inherit", "currentColor", "none", "white", "unset", "/^var\\(--/"]
```

Anything matching `^var\(--` satisfies it. `color: var(--totally-made-up)` passes
`lint:css`, passes `tsc`, and ships — rendering as an invalid value the browser
drops, which usually reads as "inherited colour" rather than as an error.

`web/src/index.css` is additionally in `ignoreFiles`, so the definitions file is
not linted either.

## How it surfaced

While building the Stage 5–8 dictionary rows (#260 / PR #275) I reached for
`var(--border-subtle)` and `var(--surface-raised)`. Neither exists in
`index.css`. `lint:css` was green. I caught them by hand, and the merged code
does not contain them.

## Current state: no live defect

A full diff of defined vs. used tokens on `main` (c6904b9) comes out clean:

```
defined in index.css: 116    used elsewhere: 112    used-but-undefined: 0
```

So this is a gap, not an outage — and a gate added now starts green and stays
meaningful, which is the good time to add one.

## Proposed fix

A small offline check, in the same spirit as the other `web/` drift checks:

1. Parse `--token:` definitions from `web/src/index.css`.
2. Parse `var(--token)` uses from every other `.css` file under `web/src`.
3. Fail on any use with no definition. Report the token and the files using it.

Roughly the 15 lines of Python/Node used to produce the numbers above. Wire it
into `npm run verify` next to `lint:css`.

### Notes for whoever picks it up

- **Respect `var(--x, fallback)`.** A use with a fallback is not necessarily a
  defect; decide explicitly whether to allow it, and say which in the code.
- Tokens can be defined outside `:root` (media queries, `[data-theme]` blocks) —
  scrape all of `index.css`, not just the `:root` block.
- **Prove it can fail before trusting it** (standing repo rule): plant
  `var(--nope)` in a component stylesheet and confirm the check goes red. A gate
  that has only ever been green is not evidence.
- The reverse direction (116 defined vs 112 used → some tokens unused) is a
  *separate*, weaker idea. Unused tokens may be a deliberate palette; do not fail
  the build on them without deciding that first.

## Scope

One new script under `web/scripts/`, one line in `package.json`. No CSS changes.

issues.title: Dictionary ValueSet canonicals are gated but barely rendered — link them, and show Binding.value
issues.bodyMd:
Follow-up from #260 / PR #275, and a natural pickup alongside #264.

## The mismatch

`check-catalog-integrity.mjs` gates that every SPiER-local `valueSet:` canonical
in the dictionary resolves to a generated `ValueSet-<id>.json`. The gate is
correct and worth keeping. Its stated rationale, however, describes a rendering
that does not exist:

> A `valueSet` pointing at nothing would render as a bindable set on the page
> while the IG published no such set — the same class of unbacked claim as a dead
> code link, so it is gated the same way.

What the page actually does with the 19 `valueSet:` canonicals in
`dataElements.ts`:

| Field | Gated? | Rendered? |
|---|---|---|
| `Concept.code` / `Binding.code` | yes | yes — `CodeLink` → `/ig/CodeSystem-<id>.html` |
| `Concept.valueSet` | yes | as **plain `<code>` text**, not a link (`DataDictionary.tsx:172`) |
| `Binding.value.valueSet` | yes | **not rendered at all** |

So the "dead code link" analogy holds only for `code`. A `Concept.valueSet` cannot
404, because nothing links to it. A `Binding.value.valueSet` cannot mislead a
reader, because no reader ever sees it.

## Why it matters

Two directions, and they point the same way:

1. **The value side is the interesting half and it is invisible.** #260's whole
   premise was that SPiER's characteristic move is an Observation coded with one
   concept and *valued* from a different vocabulary. The schema now models that
   (`Binding.value = { kind, system?, valueSet? }`, 24 blocks), the gate protects
   it, and the page shows none of it. An implementer reading the dictionary still
   cannot see what vocabulary a value is drawn from.
2. **A gate justified by a rendering that doesn't exist will drift.** Nobody
   reading that comment can check it against the page. Either the page should
   render and link these, or the comment should stop claiming it does.

## Proposal

Prefer fixing the page, not the comment:

- [ ] Link `Concept.valueSet` → `/ig/ValueSet-<id>.html` (the generated file the
      gate already proves exists), same treatment as `CodeLink` gives a code.
- [ ] Surface `Binding.value` in the bindings table — at minimum `kind`, and the
      `valueSet` / `system` when present, linked where SPiER-local.
- [ ] Once rendered, update the gate's comment to describe what is actually on the
      page.

`codeHref` (`dataElements.ts:139`) already centralizes system → URL mapping; a
`valueSetHref` sibling is the obvious shape.

## Relationship to #264

#264 wants per-binding **fidelity** (`wider` / `relatedto`) rendered, derived from
the ConceptMap. That is the same table, the same column area, and the same "make
the value side legible" goal. If #264 is picked up first, fold this in; if this is
picked up first, leave the fidelity column stubbed. Doing them in either order is
fine — doing them independently means touching the bindings table twice.

## Not a live defect

Every canonical in the dictionary currently resolves (`check:catalog` is green:
13 CodeSystems, and the ValueSets it reports). This is about a claim being
protected but unpublished, not a broken link.

issues.title: Generate the outreach one-pager PDF in CI instead of by hand
issues.bodyMd:
## Problem

`docs/outreach/SPiER-Overview-Care-Pathway.pdf` is a hand-exported binary with no build step, and it drifted silently. When #276 renamed the org to "The SPiER Project", the HTML source was updated but the rendered PDF kept the retired "Suicide Prevention in Electronic Records" wording in its front-page kicker and back-page footer. Nothing caught it — it surfaced only because a text search happened to run across the repo three days later.

This is the failure mode CLAUDE.md keeps flagging: a hand-duplicated value with no gate. The PDF is the artifact that actually goes to sites (it was created in ee0fac8 for Billings Clinic outreach), so a stale copy is the version a prospective adopter reads.

## Proposal

Keep the HTML as the single source of truth and stop committing the binary:

1. Add a build script (`scripts/build-onepager.mjs`) that renders `docs/outreach/spier-onepager-source.html` to PDF with headless Chrome.
2. Run it in CI on any change to the HTML, and publish the result at a stable location — a release asset, or a fixed path served by the existing Worker via Static Assets.
3. Remove `SPiER-Overview-Care-Pathway.pdf` from git once the published copy has a durable URL.

Drift then becomes structurally impossible rather than something someone has to remember.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- **A byte-comparison freshness gate will not work.** PDF output is not reproducible across Chrome versions — the same HTML produced 196200 bytes under `Skia/PDF m150` and 196076 under `m151`. A "does the committed PDF match a fresh render" check would go red on every runner image bump. This is the main argument for generating-and-publishing (above) over keeping the binary in git behind a verify step.
- **Chrome writes the PDF and then does not exit.** The invocation has to be killed once the file appears, or the CI step hangs until the job timeout. See cea0f91 for the exact flags.
- **Local PDF tooling is absent on at least one dev machine** (no `pdftoppm` / `mutool` / `gs`; `sips` rasterizes page 1 only). If the acceptance check below needs text extraction, the script should either vendor a check that works without poppler or document `brew install poppler` as a dev prerequisite.
- Chrome handled a `file://` URL containing a space fine, unlike the IG Publisher — no need to copy the tree to a space-free path.
- `ubuntu-latest` runners ship `google-chrome-stable`, so no separate browser install step should be needed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Editing a string in the HTML and pushing produces a PDF containing the new string, without anyone running Chrome by hand.
- [ ] The published PDF is reachable at a URL stable enough to put in an email.
- [ ] Output still matches the current artifact structurally: 2 pages, 612x792 (letter), Poppins subset embedded in all four weights.
- [ ] **The gate has been seen to fail.** Per the repo convention, plant a stale/wrong string and confirm CI goes red before trusting it — five silent-pass mechanisms have bitten this repo already.

## Out of scope

Serving the one-pager as a responsive web page is a separate piece of work. The HTML today is print-only — one `@page` rule, no `@media` at all, and every `.page` is a hard `width: 8.5in; height: 11in`, so it does not reflow on a phone. Making it a real page needs an `@media screen` pass with the `@page` rules left intact. Worth doing, but it does not block generating the PDF.

Follow-up from #276.

issues.title: Add the Risk Reassessment On Time measure, now that a cadence is published
issues.bodyMd:
Split out of #279 (merged in #295), which delivered the reassessment cadence itself but deliberately left this measure behind.

The deck's panel 9 lists **Risk Reassessment On Time — goal >90%**. #279 published the interval it would score against (`PlanDefinition-SPiERReassessmentSchedule`: high 7d / moderate 14d / low 30d), so the input now exists. The measure does not.

## Why this was not "one more group"

The existing seven measures ask whether an artifact exists inside a window anchored on a single index event — a transition, an episode start, a screen. This one is structurally different in three ways at once:

1. **It pairs consecutive events.** "On time" is a property of the gap between assessment N and assessment N+1, so the criterion has to sort a patient's risk-concept Observations and walk adjacent pairs. No current criterion looks at more than one instance of the same resource.
2. **The window is data, not a constant.** The 7/14/30 days come from a PlanDefinition, and the interval that applied to a given gap is the one for the tier **in force at the start of that gap** — not the patient's tier today. So the CQL has to retrieve the schedule and join it to the tier history.
3. **Tier can change mid-episode.** A patient who moved moderate → high partway through has gaps measured against different intervals, and the step-down/step-up dates are themselves risk-concept Observations.

Any of those alone would be routine. Together they are a new class of measure logic, and folding it into #279 would have put it under a review whose subject was the interval artifact.

## Scope

- [ ] A `Measure` + group in `ig/input/fsh/measure-and-share.fsh`, patient-based like the rest.
- [ ] CQL in `ig/input/cql/SPiERSuicideSaferCareMeasures.cql`. ⚠️ The IG Publisher **does** compile this (see the correction in `docs/plans/stage-8-measure-and-share.md`) — a translation error fails the build, so this is the risky half.
- [ ] A criterion implementation in `web/src/lib/measures.ts`, or `npm run check:measures` fails on the reference.
- [ ] Decide the denominator. Candidate: patients in an episode with **at least two** risk-concept Observations, since a patient with one has no gap to be late on. State it explicitly — a denominator that quietly includes single-assessment patients scores them as failures.
- [ ] Decide how a tier with no cadence behaves. `imminent` and `no-risk` publish no interval by design, so gaps in those tiers are not measurable rather than late — most likely a denominator exclusion.

## Two things worth settling first

- **Open question 4 for the deck's author** — whether the panel-5 reassessment intervals and the panel-6 consultant review cadence are one schedule or two. If one, this measure covers both; if two, the consultant side needs its own schedule artifact (phase 4).
- The deck's goal is **>90%**, and SPiER encodes numeric targets on no `Measure`. R4 has no target element; that is an open design question noted in `docs/plans/stage-8-measure-and-share.md` and is not blocking here.

## Note on demo data

Every seeded patient with a cadence is currently overdue by 1–143 days because the scenario dates are months old. This measure will therefore score near 0% once it computes — a true result about stale fixtures rather than about the logic. Worth refreshing the seed dates (adjacent to #209) before reading anything into the number.

Spec: `docs/reference/suicide-care-dashboard-spec.md` panel 9 · Plan: `docs/plans/suicide-care-dashboard.md`

issues.title: Scenario dates are 3–5 months stale, so the demo reads as a failing pathway
issues.bodyMd:
Every clinical date in `web/src/data/population/scenarios/patient-*.json` sits 3–5 months in the past, and the demo now has enough time-relative logic that this reads as a **failing pathway** rather than as stale fixtures.

Measured 2026-08-11:

| file | earliest | latest |
|---|---|---|
| patient-001 | 2026-03-13 | 2026-03-23 |
| patient-002 … 007 | 2026-05-06 | 2026-05-20 |
| patient-008 | 2026-04-21 | 2026-05-20 |
| patient-009 | 2026-05-07 | 2026-07-20 |
| patient-010 | 2026-04-02 | 2026-07-25 |
| patient-011 | 2026-05-21 | 2026-05-30 |

40 distinct dates, spanning 2026-03 → 2026-07. (patient-009 also carries a `2027-07-20`, which is **correct** — a one-year Consent validity period, not a typo.)

## What it currently makes the demo say

Not cosmetic. Four separate surfaces report a problem that is an artifact of the fixture dates:

1. **Reassessment tracker (#279) reads uniformly red.** 7 of 11 patients are overdue by 1 to 143 days. That is arithmetically correct against a published cadence and clinically meaningless.
2. **The amber "reassessment due in 48 hours" path is never exercised.** No seeded patient is `due-today` or `due-soon`, so that branch is covered by unit tests only — a real gap in demo coverage of a rule the deck explicitly asks for.
3. **The Follow-up view's Next Visit column is empty for all 11 patients.** `nextAppointment` is future-only and the latest seeded appointment is 2026-07-24, so every row reads "No visit booked" and the view looks broken rather than empty.
4. **"New positive PHQ-9 item 9 today" is permanently 0.** It counts item-9 Observations dated today, and none can be.

Plus: #296 (`Risk Reassessment On Time`) will score near 0% the moment it computes, for this reason and not for a logic reason. Worth fixing **before** that measure lands, or its first result will be misread.

## The actual decision: re-date, or stop hardcoding a clock

This is not just "bump the dates" — that buys a few months and returns. Three options, and the tradeoffs are real:

**A. Re-date the fixtures to fixed dates near a chosen today.**
Simplest, keeps the JSON static and therefore keeps `check:scenarios` and `validate-fhir.mjs` validating exactly what the app renders. Goes stale again on the same schedule; the demo silently rots between refreshes.

**B. Offset dates relative to `now` at load time.**
Evergreen, but it breaks the property that makes the current gates meaningful: the validated artifact would no longer be the artifact the app shows, and both scenario gates plus the HL7 validator read the static files. Also interacts badly with `_savedAt` and with resources read back from a SMART server.

**C. Give the demo an anchored clock.**
Keep fixtures static and validated; let the app resolve "now" through one injectable source rather than `new Date()`. Most of the derivation code already threads a `now` parameter — `deriveRegistryRow`, `reassessmentState`, `trailingPeriod`, `deriveAppointmentTracking` all take one — so the plumbing is largely present. Costs a decision about what the demo's "today" means and a way to surface it so a viewer is not misled about the current date.

**Recommendation: C, falling back to A.** C is where the existing `now` parameters were already heading, and it is the only option that keeps the fixtures both static and current. If C is too much for now, A is worth doing anyway before #296.

## Scope

- [ ] Pick an option above and record the reasoning (this is the substance of the task).
- [ ] Whichever is picked, the four surfaces listed above must show a **mix** of states afterwards — at minimum one patient `due-today`, one `due-soon`, one on time, and one with a booked future appointment. A refresh that leaves everything overdue has not fixed anything.
- [ ] `npm run check:scenarios` and `node scripts/validate-fhir.mjs` stay green, and stay meaningful: if the app renders shifted dates, say plainly what the gates are and are not validating.
- [ ] Preserve the intra-scenario *intervals*. The relative spacing carries clinical meaning — the 48-hour outreach in patient-011's ED walkthrough, the 7-day follow-up in patient-001 — so dates must move together, not independently.
- [ ] Keep the walkthrough narration in `walkthrough` consistent with whatever the Encounter and artifact dates become.

## Related

- #279 / #295 introduced the reassessment cadence that surfaced this.
- #296 will be misread if this is not fixed first.
- #209 seeded the original cohort; this is the maintenance follow-on.

issues.title: Refreshed scenario fixtures never reach a browser that already seeded its store
issues.bodyMd:
Found while doing #297 (#300): refreshing the scenario fixtures **does not reach a browser that has already used the demo.**

`localDataSource` seeds a patient's slice from `POPULATION_SCENARIOS` on first read of a missing slice, and never again. Its own header states the constraint and the reason:

> These keys and shapes MUST NOT change — existing browsers must keep their data. Auto-seeding of population scenarios happens on first read of a missing slice (idempotent: once a slice exists, even mutated, it never reseeds).

That reasoning is sound — a user's own submitted assessments live in the same slice, so a blind reseed would destroy their work. The consequence is that **any returning visitor keeps whatever fixture version they first loaded, forever**, including on the deployed demo.

## How it showed up

While verifying #300 the browser kept rendering "Overdue by 143 days" while vitest, reading the same files, reported "Overdue by 3 days". A full dev-server restart did not change it. The stale copy was a 93 KB `spier-patient-store` in localStorage. Clearing that key made the refresh appear immediately.

So the date refresh in #300 is real but its reach is narrower than it looks, and nothing surfaces that to a viewer.

## What is actually needed

A way to re-seed **untouched** patients while leaving modified ones alone. The straightforward shape:

- [ ] Record a seed version on the slice at seed time (e.g. a `_seed` marker carrying a `SEED_VERSION` constant).
- [ ] Clear that marker on any `updateSlice` for that patient — the slice is now the user's, not the fixture's.
- [ ] On construct, re-seed any slice whose marker is present and stale. A slice with no marker is user-modified and is never touched.
- [ ] Bump `SEED_VERSION` whenever the scenarios change materially — and decide whether that bump is manual or derived (a hash of the scenario module would not need remembering).

## Constraints worth respecting

- **Never destroy user-entered data.** A demo visitor who filled in a PHQ-9 and comes back should still see it. This is the whole reason the current behaviour exists.
- **Do not change `STORE_KEY` or the slice shape** as a shortcut. Bumping the key would "work" by orphaning every existing store, which is the same as deleting user data without saying so.
- The marker is a slice-level scalar, not a resource, so it should not leak into the FHIR buckets. `validate-fhir.mjs` strips `_savedAt` from resources and reads files rather than localStorage, so it is unaffected — but confirm rather than assume.

## Worth considering alongside

A visible affordance for "reset this demo to fresh data". Today the only way to get current fixtures is to know that `spier-patient-store` exists and clear it by hand — which no viewer of the deployed demo will do. Even with the version marker, a deliberate reset is useful for anyone who has mutated a patient and wants the curated scenario back.

## Related

- #297 / #300 — the date refresh whose reach this limits.
- #279 / #295 — the reassessment cadence that made stale dates visible in the first place.

issues.title: Nothing validates the FHIR the app emits at runtime
issues.bodyMd:
Surfaced while implementing #263 phase 4 (PR #291).

## The gap

Hand-authored FHIR is well gated. **Runtime-emitted FHIR is not gated at all.**

| Source | Checked by |
|---|---|
| `ig/input/fsh/` | sushi, `validate-fhir.mjs`, IG Publisher |
| `FHIR-Resources/` | `validate-fhir.mjs` |
| `web/src/data/population/scenarios/` | `check:scenarios` + `validate-fhir.mjs` |
| **what the app creates at runtime** | **nothing — only whatever unit tests happen to assert** |

The mappers (`web/src/lib/observationMappers/`, `carePlanMappers/`), the workflow
recorders, `lib/encounters.ts` and `lib/riskEpisode.ts` all emit resources that
claim `meta.profile`. Nothing verifies those resources actually conform to the
profiles they claim.

## This is not hypothetical

Two real defects, both invisible to every existing gate:

1. **#220** — seven fabricated/misused LOINC codes emitted by
   `observationMappers/` on every generated Observation. Fixed only after manual
   review; the nightly `check:codings` was built afterwards specifically because
   *nothing validated code literals in TypeScript*.
2. **#263 phase 3/4** — `spier-episode-trigger-on-positive-screen` made the
   `episode-trigger` extension required when entry reason is `positive-screen`.
   `positive-screen` is the **first, default option** in `RiskEpisodeView`'s
   dropdown, so from the moment #289 merged, the manual recorder produced a
   non-conformant episode on every unmodified submit. Caught by reading the code
   while building phase 4 — not by any check. Fixed in #291.

The second one is the sharper illustration: a *profile invariant* was added and the
runtime immediately violated it, and CI stayed green because the validator never
sees runtime output.

## Proposal

A gate that builds representative resources through the real production code paths
and runs them past the HL7 validator.

1. A script (or vitest suite) that calls the actual builders — `deriveFromResponse`
   for each instrument, each CarePlan mapper, `buildEpisode`, `buildEncounter`,
   `buildFlag`, the Stage-5/6 recorders — with representative inputs.
2. Write the output to a temp directory, shaped the way
   `validate-fhir.mjs`'s `collectScenarioResources` already does for scenarios.
3. Run the HL7 validator over it, reusing `scripts/lib/validator-jar.mjs`.
4. Gate in CI. Java is already available in `ig.yml`'s `validate` job, so this
   could extend that job rather than adding a new one.

### Notes for whoever picks it up

- **The inputs are the hard part**, not the plumbing. A representative
  QuestionnaireResponse per instrument already exists in the scenarios — reuse
  those rather than authoring new ones (and see #263 phase 4, where a hand-written
  ASQ fixture silently derived zero Observations because the canonical and answer
  shapes were subtly wrong).
- Cover the branches that *change* the output shape, not just the happy path: the
  positive vs negative screen, an episode with and without a trigger, a
  DocumentReference (whose encounter reference is nested at `context.encounter`).
- **Prove it can fail before trusting it** (standing repo rule): revert the
  `RiskEpisodeView` trigger guard from #291 and confirm the gate goes red on the
  invariant. That is a known-real defect, so it is the ideal test case.
- Offline-reproducibility: the validator runs `-tx n/a` elsewhere in this repo, so
  external codes stay the nightly's job. Keep that split.

## Scope

New script + CI wiring. No production-code changes expected — though if the gate
finds something, that is the point.

issues.title: p007-stanley-brown is a stub named after a profile it does not conform to
issues.bodyMd:
Surfaced while implementing #263 phase 5a (PR #293).

## The problem

`p007-stanley-brown` in `web/src/data/population/scenarios/patient-007.json` is
titled **"Stanley-Brown Safety Plan"** and its id says the same. It is not one.

Current keys: `resourceType`, `id`, `status`, `intent`, `subject`, `title`,
`category`, `addresses`, `note`, `encounter`, `_savedAt`.

**There is no `activity`.** A Stanley-Brown safety plan is *entirely* its
activities — the warning signs, internal coping strategies, people and places for
distraction, people to ask for help, professionals to contact, and means
restriction. This resource carries a title and a note and nothing else.

Compare the two siblings that are real: `p001-stanley-brown` and
`p011-stanley-brown` both claim
`meta.profile = http://spier.org/StructureDefinition/spier-stanley-brown-safety-plan`
and satisfy it. `p007-stanley-brown` claims no profile — which is why the gap went
unnoticed.

## How it surfaced

#263 phase 5a replaced the CarePlan id-substring regex (`/stanley-brown/i` and
three siblings) with a `meta.profile` → stage map. This resource had been getting
its pathway stage **purely because its id contains "stanley-brown"** — exactly the
inference that epic exists to delete.

Adding the profile its name implies failed the offline gate immediately:

```
✗ scenarios/patient-007.json carePlans[0] (p007-stanley-brown): CarePlan.activity is
    required by http://spier.org/StructureDefinition/spier-stanley-brown-safety-plan
    but is absent
✗ scenarios/patient-007.json carePlans[0] (p007-stanley-brown): CarePlan.activity.detail.code
    is required by …spier-stanley-brown-safety-plan but is absent
```

So the profile claim would have been false. PR #293 gave it an explicit
pathway-stage `category` coding instead — the same mechanism the other four
scenario CarePlans use — which keeps stage resolution correct **without** asserting
conformance it does not have. That was the minimal honest fix, not a complete one.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

`patient-007`'s episode enters on `elevated-assessment`, and the scenario has **no
assessment artifact at all** — this stub is its only CarePlan. That is why #263
phase 3 had to scope its invariant (`spier-episode-trigger-on-positive-screen`) to
`positive-screen` only: widening it to `elevated-assessment` would either fail the
build on this patient or invite a fabricated artifact to satisfy it. So this fixture
is currently *limiting how strong an invariant the IG can assert*.

## Options

1. **Fill it in.** Give it real `activity` entries with
   `cams-careplan-section`-style section codes and claim the profile, matching
   `p001` / `p011`. Makes patient-007 a complete safety-planning story and lets
   phase 3's invariant be widened later.
2. **Rename it.** If patient-007 is meant to be a patient whose safety plan is
   *not yet done*, the id and title should say so (`p007-safety-plan-pending`), and
   the narrative should match. Cheapest, and arguably more useful — a scenario
   showing an incomplete plan has demo value.
3. **Delete it.** If it carries no narrative weight, remove it; the explicit stage
   category then has nothing to attach to and patient-007 has no CarePlan.

Option 2 is probably right, but it is a scenario-authoring decision.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `p007-stanley-brown` either conforms to the profile it names, or no longer
      names it
- [ ] `npm run check:scenarios` and `node scripts/validate-fhir.mjs` stay green
- [ ] The "every CarePlan in every shipped scenario resolves to a stage" test in
      `patientPathway.stageResolution.test.ts` stays green
- [ ] If option 1: note in #263 that `elevated-assessment` can now join the
      phase-3 invariant

issues.title: Walkthrough steps 11.7-2A/2B swap "caring contact" and "follow-up outreach"
issues.bodyMd:
Surfaced while implementing #263 phase 5b (PR #298), which replaced the walkthrough's
string matching with real FHIR references — making the mismatch visible for the first
time.

## The mismatch

In `web/src/data/population/scenarios/patient-011.json`, two walkthrough steps use
"caring contact" and "follow-up outreach" the **opposite** way round from the
Communications they reference:

| Step | Step title | References | Artifact's own `category.text` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `11.7-2A` | "24–48h **caring-contact** call scheduled" | `Communication/p011-outreach-48h` | "Follow-up **outreach** attempt" |
| `11.7-2B` | "7-day **follow-up outreach** + risk recheck" | `Communication/p011-caring-contact` | "**Caring contact**" |

So the chart renders step "24–48h caring-contact call" with a linked artifact
labelled "Follow-up outreach attempt", and vice versa. Both read as a mistake even
though the links are right.

## The references are correct — the dates settle it

Episode start is `2026-05-21`:

- `p011-outreach-48h` — `sent: 2026-05-23`, **two days** out → this is the 24–48h
  contact → step `11.7-2A`
- `p011-caring-contact` — `sent: 2026-05-30`, **nine days** out → this is the ~7-day
  contact → step `11.7-2B`

That also matches the artifacts' own `category.text` and the usual clinical meaning
(a caring contact is a brief non-demanding contact at intervals post-discharge; a
24–48h call is an outreach attempt). PR #298 assigned the references on that basis
and deliberately did **not** edit either side, since choosing one to "fix" is a guess
about intent.

## What to decide

One of these, not both:

1. **Fix the step titles** to match the artifacts (and standard usage):
   `11.7-2A` → "24–48h follow-up outreach call", `11.7-2B` → "7-day caring contact
   + risk recheck". Smallest change; makes the rendered chart coherent.
2. **Fix the artifacts** — rename/re-categorise the Communications so
   `p011-caring-contact` is the 48h one. Requires moving the dates too, since the
   dates are what currently make the assignment unambiguous, and would ripple into
   the Stage-6/8 follow-up measures that read these by timing.
3. **Neither** — decide the terms are genuinely interchangeable in this narrative
   and leave it. Then the rendered mismatch is cosmetic and this can be closed as
   won't-fix.

Option 1 looks right, but the ED scenario narration traces to
`docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.md` and the step labels (`11.7-2A`) map to that
document, so whoever owns that mapping should confirm the wording rather than have
it changed underneath them.

⚠️ Check `docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.md` before renaming — if the step titles
were lifted verbatim from it, the doc needs the same edit or the two drift apart.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Decision recorded (which side moved, or won't-fix with the reason)
- [ ] `docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.md` consistent with whatever is chosen
- [ ] `npm run verify` green — in particular `check:scenarios`, whose walkthrough-ref
      check would catch a reference broken while re-shuffling
- [ ] If the Communications' dates move: re-check the Stage-6 follow-up timeliness
      and caring-contact adherence measures, which read these by timing

issues.title: Assessment pages carry two titles, and heading order runs h2 → h1
issues.bodyMd:
Fallout from #319, which put the assessment and workflow form views on the shared page template. Filed rather than fixed there, because the honest fix is upstream. ## What happens On the 18 assessment routes, the page renders our `PageHeader` title and then `@formbox/renderer` renders the Questionnaire's own `title` as an `

` inside the card. `/patient/assessments/phq-9`, live: ```html

PHQ-9 Depression Screening

Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9)

``` Those are the only two headings above the form. So: - **Heading order goes backwards.** The document's first heading is level 2 and its second jumps up to level 1. Someone navigating by heading gets a structure that doesn't nest — a real structure defect, though not a hard WCAG success-criterion failure. - **Two titles, same size.** Both compute to 24px, so it reads as redundancy rather than as hierarchy, even though the strings say different things (the SPiER tool name vs. the FHIR artifact's own title). Before #319 these pages had no page header at all, so the renderer's `

` was the page's only heading and both problems were invisible. ## Where - `web/src/components/QuestionnaireView.tsx` — 17 assessment routes - `web/src/components/StanleyBrownView.tsx` — 1 ## Why #319 left it `RendererProperties` in `@formbox/renderer@0.2.1` is `{ questionnaire, defaultQuestionnaireResponse, defaultLanguage, onChange, onSubmit, onLanguageChange, terminologyServerUrl, fhirVersion, theme }` — nothing controls whether the title renders or at what level. Every workaround available on our side is worse than the defect: 1. **Ask upstream for the prop** (`renderTitle={false}`, or a heading-level offset). Correct fix; not ours to make. Repo: https://github.com/HealthSamurai/formbox-renderer 2. **Strip `title` from the questionnaire before passing it.** Removes the `

`, but the renderer's description paragraph is then headerless, and it means handing the renderer an altered resource — in an app whose whole argument is fidelity to the FHIR artifact. 3. **Demote it with CSS.** Cosmetic only; the semantics stay wrong. And the class name is build-hashed (`t1n83i42`), so the only stable selector is the element itself (`.form-card h1`) — styling third-party DOM by tag. 4. **Make `PageHeader` render `

`.** Arguably right on its own merits: the four lenses currently start at `

` with no `

` anywhere on the page. But on these 18 routes it would produce two `

`s instead of a bad order, so it only helps once (1) lands. ## Nothing gates this `npm run check:template` forbids a raw `

` in our own pages and form views, which is what keeps the page title single. It says nothing about heading *order*, and cannot see markup that a dependency emits. If this gets fixed, the check to add is over rendered output, not source text. ## Suggested resolution Open the upstream request for a title/heading-level prop, and revisit (4) — `PageHeader` as `

` app-wide — once it exists, so the two changes land together and the page ends up with exactly one `

` at the top. ## Repro 1. `cd web && npm run dev` 2. Open `#/patient/assessments/phq-9` (any assessment route does it) 3. `document.querySelectorAll('.ehr-content-body h1, .ehr-content-body h2')` → `[h2.page-header__title, h1]`

issues.title: Lethal-means measure scores "could not be done" and "not yet due" as misses
issues.bodyMd:
## What happened

Adding the three ED exception-branch patients in #318 dropped **Lethal Means Counseling Completed** from **2/5 (40%)** to **2/7 (29%)**. The arithmetic is correct and the engine agrees with the published definition — `check:measures` is green. The problem is what the definition can express.

Of the nine measure groups, only two moved:

| Group | Before | After | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Current risk level documented | 4/5 · 80% | 6/7 · 86% | ↑ correct — both new episode patients have a documented risk level |
| Lethal means counseling | 2/5 · 40% | **2/7 · 29%** | ↓ this issue |
| The other seven | unchanged | unchanged | correct — they key off a care transition or a referral, and neither patient has one |

`patient-012` (negative screen) correctly contributes to no denominator at all: no episode opens, so she is absent from every cohort.

## Why the two new misses are not process failures

`Measure/lethal-means-counseling` has:

- **denominator** — `Has An Active Suicide Safer Care Episode`
- **denominator-exclusion** — `Episode Closed Administratively`

Both new patients have active episodes and neither received counseling, so both count as misses. But:

- **`patient-013` (Owen Delacroix)** was **transferred to inpatient psychiatry**. Means counseling belongs at discharge to the community — the receiving facility's step. His episode is open and the counseling **is not yet due**.
- **`patient-014` (Terrence Whitfield)** **eloped at 02:35** while on 1:1 precautions. There was **no opportunity** to counsel him.

Neither is a failure of the ED's means-counseling workflow, and the measure has no way to say so. A site reading 29% would conclude the workflow is broken when two of the five misses are structural.

## What I deliberately did not do

Closing `patient-014`'s episode administratively would have excluded him and lifted the score. That would be wrong twice over: he still needs follow-up, so the episode belongs open, and it would also drop him from **Current Risk Level Documented**, which he legitimately passes. Massaging demo data to flatter a measure is the opposite of what the measure layer is for.

## Options

1. **Add a denominator exclusion** for episodes where the patient transferred to a higher level of care, or left before disposition. Cleanest, and mirrors how the follow-up measures already exclude via `Excluded From Follow Up Measurement`. Needs a coded reason on the episode or the encounter disposition — `Encounter.hospitalization.dischargeDisposition` already carries `psy` and `aadvice` on these two patients, so the signal exists.
2. **Give the measure a "not yet due" concept**, so an open episode with no discharge event is neither numerator nor miss. More faithful, more work, and it changes the shape of the report.

Option 1 handles the elopement case well and the transfer case adequately. Option 2 is the better answer for transfer specifically, since the counseling genuinely is still owed — by someone else.

This is a **specification question, not a bug**: the CQL, the engine and the published Measure all agree with each other. Whichever way it goes, the exclusion or the new population needs to land in `ig/input/fsh/measure-and-share.fsh`, in `ig/input/cql/SPiERSuicideSaferCareMeasures.cql`, and in the `CRITERIA` table in `web/src/lib/measures.ts` together — `npm run check:measures` gates that they stay in step.

## Reproducing

```bash
cd web && npm run dev
```

Then `#/guide/measures`, or read the per-patient membership by evaluating `evaluateAllMeasures` over `POPULATION_SCENARIOS`.

Found while auditing the dashboard after #318 and #320 completed the ED scenario demo (37/37 steps narrated across `patient-011` through `patient-014`).

issues.title: Clinical review: ED Scenario 11 — 10 proposed steps, 3 new patient courses, and one open note
issues.bodyMd:
Clinical review of the ED Suicide-Care scenario (Behavioral Health Scenario 11) before it goes to the HL7 BH working group. **@Kelly** — everything below is a decision only you can make; none of it is blocked on code.

Three things to look at, in rough priority order.

---

## 1. Ten proposed steps — accept or reject each

The circulated workbook had 27 steps. SPiER proposes 10 more, closing three gaps in the original: **the patient is never an actor**, **there are no alternate or exception flows**, and **consent appears as an input but never as a step**.

Every one is marked `(proposed)` wherever it appears, so nothing presents them as the working group's own work. Rejecting any is cheap — they come out of one JSON file and the workbook regenerates.

- [ ] **`11.2-1C` — Complete a self-administered suicide risk screener on a patient-facing device**
  *Patient (or caregiver) / Respondent.* The scenario permits patient self-report in 11.2-1A but never gives the patient an Actor row, so nothing distinguishes a self-completed screen — including whether the patient was alone when answering, which changes how the answers should be read.
- [ ] **`11.2-1D` — Document a declined, deferred, or incompletable screen**
  *Triage Nurse / Screener.* A blank is currently indistinguishable from a negative screen. That difference drives both the clinical follow-up and the denominator of every screening measure.
- [ ] **`11.2-2D` — Close the loop on a negative screen**
  *EHR System / Router.* 11.2-2A defines three outcomes but only the positive ones are consumed anywhere. A negative screen still has consequences: a re-screen interval, and the standing ability of a clinician to escalate anyway.
- [ ] **`11.5-1D` — Arrange psychiatric admission or transfer when ED discharge is not appropriate**
  *ED Provider (MD/APP) / Disposition Manager.* 11.5's own preamble describes patients awaiting psychiatric placement or transfer, but every step after it follows the discharge-home branch. The placement itself — and the log of failed attempts that explains a long boarding stay — is unmodelled.
- [ ] **`11.5-1E` — Manage elopement or departure against advice by a patient at risk**
  *ED Nurse / Charge Nurse / Safety Monitor.* A patient on suicide precautions who leaves is among the highest-risk events an ED sees, and the scenario has no path for it. With no modelled event the encounter simply closes, and the follow-up protocol in 11.7 never fires.
- [ ] **`11.6-1C` — Review, contribute to, and accept the safety plan**
  *Patient (with support person, if present) / Collaborator.* The scenario calls the plan collaborative but models only the clinician side. A safety plan the patient did not actually agree to is a documented artifact rather than an intervention — and naming a support person the patient has not agreed to name is itself a disclosure.
- [ ] **`11.6-2C` — Commit to and carry out the agreed means-safety actions**
  *Patient and/or caregiver / Means-Safety Participant.* 11.6-2A documents that counseling happened and what was agreed, but nothing owns the actions or closes them out. Means-safety is the intervention with the strongest evidence base here, and "agreed" is not "done".
- [ ] **`11.6-3B` — Apply release and confidentiality rules before portal delivery**
  *EHR System / Release Manager.* For an adolescent whose guardian holds proxy access, or a plan naming a member of the household the patient is unsafe with, automatic portal release can be the harm. Real deployments gate this, and the scenario should say so rather than describing release as automatic.
- [ ] **`11.7-0A` — Capture consent and privacy directives before any disclosure**
  *ED Clinician / Consent and Privacy Manager.* Consent appears only as an input to 11.7-1A and 11.7-1B. Whether the packet may lawfully be sent is a decision with an actor, a timestamp, and a record — and for a minor or a Part 2 program it can forbid the transmission the scenario assumes.
- [ ] **`11.7-2D` — Respond to post-discharge outreach, or not**
  *Patient (or caregiver) / Follow-Up Participant.* 11.7-2C escalates on missed follow-up, but nothing models the patient side of the contact. "No answer" and "asked us to stop" are clinically and legally different, and only one of them should escalate.

⚠️ **The EHR-S FM references on these ten are drafts** — `IN.1.9` and `DC.3.2` especially — and need checking against the published function list. So, in fairness, does every other reference in that document, which still calls itself a first-pass skeleton.

---

## 2. Three clinical courses — sanity-check

The demo now runs four ED patients so the exception branches can be shown rather than described. **The clinical detail in the last three is mine, not a clinician's.** Timings, the placement log, the deferred-screen reason, the elopement-at-handoff detail — all plausible, none reviewed by anyone who has worked an ED.

| Patient | Course | Worth checking |
|---|---|---|
| [Maria Alvarez](https://spier-adoption-guide.bbthorson.workers.dev/#/patient/chart/patient-011) | Non-acute positive → safety plan → discharge → follow-up | The original scenario; unchanged except the five proposed steps |
| [Nia Barrett](https://spier-adoption-guide.bbthorson.workers.dev/#/patient/chart/patient-012) | Self-administered ASQ, **negative**, discharged | Is a 12-month re-screen interval right for a negative ED screen? |
| [Owen Delacroix](https://spier-adoption-guide.bbthorson.workers.dev/#/patient/chart/patient-013) | Screen **deferred** for altered mental status, re-attempted, acute positive, 6h board, **transferred** | Is deferring at triage and re-attempting when alert what actually happens? Is a four-facility placement log realistic? |
| [Terrence Whitfield](https://spier-adoption-guide.bbthorson.workers.dev/#/patient/chart/patient-014) | Acute positive, 1:1 precautions, **eloped** at 02:35 | Two unanswered calls, and the emergency contact **not** called because no consent is on file — is that the right call, or does policy override? |

Open each chart and read the **Scenario walkthrough** section. Steps tagged `proposed step` are the additions from §1.

---

## 3. Your own note on 11.2-2B is still open

From the original workbook, on the Event cell of `11.2-2B`:

> **Kelly Samuelson, 2026-02-19:** "storyboard - need the vendor agnostic version of this and then EHR specialist can translate this per EHR"

Still unresolved. The step's text is *"Communicate suicide screening status to the ED team (trackboard + chart banner)"*, which is vendor-flavoured language in a document meant to be vendor-neutral. A vendor-agnostic rewording would be a drop-in edit.

That note was **silently dropped by the CSV export** of the workbook — CSV has nowhere to put a comment. It now lives in the source JSON's `reviewNotes` and renders as a visible column on the mapping sheet, so it cannot vanish again.

---

## The artifacts

- **The workbook** (download button, top right) — https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/blob/main/docs/use-cases/dist/HL7_BH_USE_CASES-ED-Scenario-11.xlsx
- **The FHIR / functional mapping**, incl. a *Proposed additions* section — https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/blob/main/docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.md
- **How it all fits together** — https://github.com/SPiER-Project/adoption-guide/blob/main/docs/use-cases/README.md

## How to give feedback

Comment here, or annotate anything. **Do not edit the .xlsx** — it is generated from `docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.json` and the next build discards hand edits. That is deliberate: it is what stopped the demo, the mapping doc and the workbook from drifting apart, which they already had.

## Related

- #324 — a separate measure-specification decision (lethal-means counseling scoring transfer and elopement as misses)
- Built in #312, #313, #315, #318, #320

issues.title: C-SSRS and CAMS-B mappers read valueBoolean, but the forms emit coded Yes/No — an endorsed screen derives "no risk"
issues.bodyMd:
Found while implementing #230 (foreign C-SSRS recognition), which needed to know what shape the C-SSRS mappers actually read.

## Observed, not inferred

A C-SSRS screener filled in through the app's own form — q1 Yes, q2 Yes, **q5 Yes ("specific plan and intent")** — derives:

```
tier: 'none'   alert: 'none'   summary: "C-SSRS: No risk identified"
```

The highest-acuity answer on the instrument produces a clean screen. Two independent confirmations:

1. The form's own **Live FHIR QuestionnaireResponse** panel shows the answers as codings, exactly as the Questionnaire declares them:
   ```json
   "linkId": "q1",
   "answer": [ { "valueCoding": { "system": "http://snomed.info/sct", "code": "373066001", "display": "Yes" } } ]
   ```
2. Feeding a QR in that exact shape to `mapCSSRSScreener` returns tier `none` / `"C-SSRS: No risk identified"`.

## Root cause

`getBooleanAnswer` (`shared.ts`) reads **only** `answer.valueBoolean`:

```ts
export function getBooleanAnswer(item) { return item?.answer?.[0]?.valueBoolean }
```

But **not one Questionnaire in this repo declares a `boolean` item.** Every yes/no question is `type: choice` with SNOMED Yes (`373066001`) / No (`373067005`) `answerOption`s — checked across all 13 instrument Questionnaires. So every `getBooleanAnswer` call site silently reads `undefined`, which the risk ladders treat as "not endorsed".

The repo already contains the correct reader — `getYesNoBoolean`, which decodes exactly those two SNOMED codes — and the mappers split cleanly by which one they use:

| Mapper | Reader | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `cssrsScreener.ts` (9 calls) — and via `mapCSSRSScreenerCore`: **Screener, Pediatric, Since-Last-Contact** | `getBooleanAnswer` | ❌ broken |
| `cssrsFull.ts` (13 calls) | `getBooleanAnswer` | ❌ broken |
| `camsSectionB.ts` — `ideation-present`, `plan-present` (both `choice` with Yes/No) | `getBooleanAnswer` | ❌ broken |
| `asq.ts`, `pss3.ts`, `safet.ts` | `getYesNoBoolean` | ✅ fine |

## Why no gate caught it

Three blind spots lined up, and it is worth fixing that too, not just the reader:

- **The mapper tests construct the wrong shape.** `cssrsScreener.test.ts` opens with `// C-SSRS Screener items are plain booleans (getBooleanAnswer)` and builds `valueBoolean` QRs — so the suite proves the mapper works on input the app never produces.
- **No scenario fixture exercises it.** No `patient-*.json` carries a C-SSRS or CAMS-Section-B QuestionnaireResponse *with items*, so `check:scenarios:responses` — which does validate answers against the Questionnaire, including `value[x]` type — never sees one of these forms.
- **The #230 fallback path masks it in the one place it is tested.** `fallbackDispatch` deliberately normalizes to `valueBoolean` because that is what the mapper reads, so a **foreign** C-SSRS payload derives the correct tier while a **native** SPiER submission does not. That inversion is the tell.

## Suggested fix

- Make the yes/no read accept both shapes — one shared helper (`getYesNoBoolean` already handles the coding; have it fall through to `valueBoolean`) and use it everywhere a `choice`-with-Yes/No item is read. That keeps #230's normalization valid, since booleans stay acceptable.
- Add a **fixture** that would have caught this: a scenario QuestionnaireResponse for the C-SSRS screener with coded answers, so `check:scenarios:responses` covers the native shape. A test alone is not enough — the existing test is what encoded the wrong assumption.
- Consider a gate asserting that each mapper's reader matches its Questionnaire's declared item `type`. That is the class-level fix; the two above are the instance.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A C-SSRS screener QR with SNOMED coded answers derives the correct tier (q5 Yes → `high`)
- [ ] Same for `cssrsFull` and `camsSectionB`'s two items
- [ ] A scenario fixture carries a coded C-SSRS QR, so `check:scenarios` sees the native shape
- [ ] `npm run verify` green, and #230's foreign-payload tests still pass (booleans must stay acceptable)

Refs #230, #220 (same class: silently wrong clinical meaning that every gate reported as fine).

issues.title: patient-011's Stanley-Brown safety plan is missing the LOINC note category 87626-8
issues.bodyMd:
Two hand-authored Stanley-Brown safety plans in the population scenarios disagree about their `category`, and one of them is almost certainly an oversight.

```
patient-001  p001-stanley-brown  [735324008, 87626-8, suicide-risk]
patient-011  p011-stanley-brown  [735324008,           suicide-risk]
```

`87626-8` is LOINC "Suicide prevention note". `patient-001` carries it, `patient-011` does not. The IG's own example Instance (`ExampleStanleyBrownSafetyPlan`) carries it too, so `patient-011` is the odd one out of three.

## How it surfaced

While adding named category slices in #325 I initially made `category[suicidePreventionNote]` **1..1** on `SPiERStanleyBrownSafetyPlan`. The HL7 validator then failed on exactly this resource:

```
CarePlan.category: minimum required = 3, but only found 2
Slice 'CarePlan.category:suicidePreventionNote': a matching slice is required, but not found
```

I set the slice to **0..1** rather than "fix" demo data I had not been asked to touch — requiring the code is a conformance decision that deserves its own call, and I did not want to make it as a side effect of a data-loss fix. So the profile is currently permissive *because* of this inconsistency.

## The decision to make

Either is defensible; they just need to be the same:

1. **Add `87626-8` to `patient-011`** and tighten the slice to `1..1`. Argues that every Stanley-Brown safety plan is a suicide prevention note, which is hard to argue against, and makes the code queryable — a consumer can find safety-plan notes by LOINC document type across the whole registry.
2. **Leave the slice `0..1`** and record that the code is optional. Argues that `735324008` (SNOMED treatment escalation plan) is the load-bearing classification and the LOINC note type is a nice-to-have.

Worth noting which way makes the resource more useful externally: the HL7/ASTP US Behavioral Health Profiles IG classifies its mental-health notes by LOINC `DocumentReference.type`, so a LOINC document-type code on the safety plan is the axis a partner is most likely to filter on. That leans toward option 1.

## Also worth checking while in there

Whether any other scenario resource has the same shape of omission — a standard category present on one patient's instance and absent from another's. #325 fixed the *mechanism* that was dropping these codes at compile time, but it did not audit the hand-authored scenario JSON for pre-existing gaps.

## Notes

- Nothing is broken today: `npm run check:scenarios` and `node scripts/validate-fhir.mjs` are both green, because the slice is `0..1`. This is a consistency and usefulness issue, not a conformance failure.
- Context: #325, and `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md`.
- The profile is `SPiERStanleyBrownSafetyPlan` in `ig/input/fsh/stanley-brown.fsh`; the ruleset is `SafetyPlanNoteAndSuicideRiskCategory` in `ig/input/fsh/concept-layer.fsh`, which carries the reasoning for the current `0..1`.

issues.title: check:codings — web/src SNOMED floor has drifted to ~1/3 of its live count (7 vs 19)
issues.bodyMd:
`check-codings.mjs` floors assert **liveness, not completeness** — "did this scan still look at this vocabulary in this source" — and CLAUDE.md sets the convention at roughly **half** the real count. One family has drifted well below that.

Measured on `9d3ef83`:

| Source | Family | Live | Floor | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `web/src` | loinc | 98 | 49 | 0.50 ✓ |
| `web/src` | **snomed** | **19** | **7** | **0.37** ⚠️ |
| `web/src` | tho | 25 | 12 | 0.48 ✓ |
| `web/src/data/catalog` | loinc | 36 | 17 | 0.47 ✓ |
| `web/src/data/catalog` | snomed | 3 | 1 | 0.33 (see below) |
| `web/src/data/catalog` | tho | 14 | 7 | 0.50 ✓ |

`web/src` SNOMED is the real one: 19 codings guarded by a floor of 7, so **12 SNOMED codings could leave the scan and the gate would stay green.** Half would be ~9–10.

The catalog SNOMED row is arithmetic, not drift — half of 3 rounds to 1 or 2, and a floor of 1 on 3 codings is about as tight as that number allows. Probably leave it; raise it to 2 if you want the ratio uniform.

## Why this needs a human call rather than a script

This is exactly the failure #232 documented: a floor that sat at a quarter of its real count while a source doubled, with nothing going red. CLAUDE.md is explicit that a growing source needs a **deliberate re-check**, because nothing re-checks it on its own. So the fix is to look at the number and choose it, not to auto-derive it — an auto-derived floor would track the count and therefore assert nothing.

Note that LOINC is fine precisely because someone did this recently: #323 raised the `web/src` LOINC floor to 49 as it added C-SSRS codes, which is why that row is at exactly 0.50. SNOMED grew in the same window (the yes/no pair `373066001`/`373067005` in `fallbackDispatch.ts`, plus other work) without its floor moving.

## Suggested change

In `SCAN` (`web/scripts/check-codings.mjs`, ~line 164):

```diff
-  { path: 'web/src', exts: ['.ts', '.tsx'], minCodings: { loinc: 49, snomed: 7, tho: 12 } },
+  { path: 'web/src', exts: ['.ts', '.tsx'], minCodings: { loinc: 49, snomed: 9, tho: 12 } },
```

Then prove it can fail before trusting it — per the repo's standing practice, delete a couple of SNOMED codings from `web/src` and confirm the gate goes red at the new floor. `npm run check:codings` needs network (tx.fhir.org) and runs nightly via `terminology-nightly.yml`, so this will not show up in `npm run verify`.

## Notes

- Not urgent and nothing is currently wrong — every one of the 72 external codings matches tx.fhir.org today. This is about how much protection the floor still provides.
- Every run prints the live count beside each floor, so any recent nightly log shows where the ratios stand.
- Context: #232 (the original stale-floor incident), #261 (why `SCAN` entries deliberately overlap), #325.

issues.title: Report the US Behavioral Health Profiles IG's build defects upstream (5 findings, 3 candidate channels)
issues.bodyMd:
Five defects in the HL7/ASTP **US Behavioral Health Profiles IG** CI build, found while aligning SPiER against it (see `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md`). All five **re-verified against the live build on 2026-08-13** — they are not stale.

Reporting them is cheap, establishes SPiER as a contributing implementer rather than a downstream consumer, and is worth doing before the SAMHSA/ASTP pilot cohort (45 exchange partners, 9 states) hardens around the current shape. Testing there completes end of 2026, with a Behavioral Health Information Resource in 2027.

## ⚠️ First: where to send them

The research doc said to "file issues on `HL7/us-behavioral-health-profiles`" and inferred from `open_issues_count: 0` that the tracker was unattended. **That was wrong** — that repo has `has_issues: False`. Issues are *disabled*, not empty. Anything filed there goes nowhere.

The IG's own footer offers three channels, which disagree with each other:

| Channel | Live? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `lantanagroup/astp-bhp` | ✅ `has_issues: true`, 1 open | The IG's own **"New Issue"** link. The authoring repo (Lantana are the authors). Last pushed 2026-02-26. |
| `HL7/us-behavioral-health-profiles` | ❌ issues disabled | Also linked from the page. Dead end. Last pushed 2026-07-22 — so the *code* moves here while feedback is directed elsewhere. |
| [ASTP Health IT Feedback and Inquiry Portal](https://inquiry.healthit.gov/support/plugins/servlet/desk/portal/2) | ? | Linked as the formal channel. Heavier weight; likely right for anything policy-adjacent. |

**Recommendation:** the technical defects go to `lantanagroup/astp-bhp` (it is the link the IG itself offers for a new issue). Note the mismatch between where code lands and where feedback is invited as its own observation — that is useful signal for them.

## The five findings

1. **Mixed US Core versions inside one build.** Profiles derive from `us-core-documentreference|7.0.0` (and reference `us-core-patient|7.0.0`, `us-core-encounter|7.0.0`, …) while the examples pin `us-core-questionnaireresponse|6.1.0`. Both `|6.1.0` and `|7.0.0` of the same profile appear in one build.
2. **The change log describes "0.2.0 Updates"; the package is `0.1.0`.**
3. **The change log's removals are not reflected in the crosswalk.** It records six data elements as removed (Adverse Event, Name to Use, Gender Identity, Sexual Orientation, Pronouns, Farmworker Status) — **all six are still live rows** in `bh_to_fhir_profiles.html` (rows 1, 69, 75, 84, 88, 111 of 113). Re-confirmed 2026-08-13. This is the highest-value one to report: an implementer reading the crosswalk as the element list builds against elements the publisher considers gone.
4. **Two canonical bases.** The `ImplementationGuide` declares `http://hl7.org/fhir/us/bhp/…`; every artifact uses `http://fhir.org/guides/astp/bhp/…`.
5. **Narrative contradicts its own examples.** `quick_facts.html` says Medicare; the story and the `Coverage-medicaid-coverage-example-1` / `Organization-fl-medicaid-example-1` examples say Florida Medicaid. Quick Facts says James requested female counselors; `full_story.html` says afternoon appointments.

## Related but filed separately

The `QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire`-points-at-a-PDF problem is a distinct, more consequential finding with a concrete offer attached, so it gets its own issue rather than being buried in a list.

## Definition of done

- Each finding submitted through whichever channel is chosen, with a link.
- The channel confusion itself raised (three links, one dead).
- `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md` §5 updated with the outcome, and its "empty tracker" inference corrected — it currently reads as though the tracker is unattended rather than disabled.

## Notes

- These are ordinary pre-ballot CI-build defects. The tone should be a contributing implementer's, not a reviewer's — none of this is unusual for `0.1.0`, and it is *why* SPiER declines a FHIR-package dependency for now (recorded in `ig/input/pagecontent/relationship-to-other-igs.md`).
- Re-verify before submitting: this is a continuously rebuilt target.

issues.title: Offer the SPiER C-SSRS Questionnaire as the canonical target for the BH IG's C-SSRS example (currently a PDF)
issues.bodyMd:
The US Behavioral Health Profiles IG's C-SSRS example sets:

```json
"questionnaire": "https://www.cms.gov/files/document/cssrs-screen-version-instrument.pdf"
```

Re-verified against the live build **2026-08-13** — still a PDF.

`QuestionnaireResponse.questionnaire` is `canonical(Questionnaire)`. Pointing it at a PDF means:

- no validation of the response against its form,
- no SDC rendering,
- no `observationExtract` / `calculatedExpression`,
- no answer-option or ordinal checking,
- and the item codes are only recoverable through the `linkId` convention (`/93246-7`), which is itself non-standard.

Their PHQ-9 example does it correctly (`http://hl7.org/fhir/us/core/Questionnaire/phq-9-example|6.1.0`), so this is an inconsistency within one IG rather than a considered position.

## Why SPiER is well placed to offer a fix

This is the clearest place SPiER is materially ahead, and the offer costs nothing:

- SPiER publishes a real C-SSRS Screener `Questionnaire` with `answerOption`, ordinal extensions and per-item `code`s.
- **Its item codes are item-for-item identical to the ones on their example** — all eight: `93246-7`, `93247-5`, `93248-3`, `93249-1`, `93250-9`, `93267-3`, `93269-9`, and `93374-7`. Nothing needs translating.
- Their example's answers (`LA32-8` / `LA33-6` from LOINC's LL361-7) are already accepted by SPiER's dispatch (#325).
- SPiER's validator gate checks every QuestionnaireResponse against its Questionnaire, so the pairing is known to hold: SPiER reads their example verbatim and recovers the same risk level the IG itself asserts (fixtures in `web/src/lib/observationMappers/__fixtures__/`).

## What to actually propose

Two options, and the second is likelier to be accepted:

1. **Point `questionnaire` at the SPiER canonical** (`http://spier.org/Questionnaire/C-SSRS-Screener`). Direct, but asks an HL7/ASTP IG to depend on a SPiER URL — a real governance ask, and premature while SPiER's own artifacts are `draft`/`experimental`.
2. **Contribute a C-SSRS `Questionnaire` to their IG**, modelled on SPiER's, so their example points at their own artifact. Keeps their guide self-contained, closes the defect properly, and still puts SPiER's modelling into a federally funded IG. Their PHQ-9 example already follows this pattern with a US Core Questionnaire.

Option 2 is the recommendation. Option 1 is the fallback if they would rather reference than adopt.

⚠️ **Licensing gate.** The C-SSRS is not public domain, and `docs/best-practices/licensing-verification-backlog.md` records that **no** SPiER instrument status has been verified against the rights holder's current published terms. Contributing a C-SSRS Questionnaire to a third-party IG is a redistribution question, not just a technical one — this must clear epic #64 before anything is offered. Do not skip that on the grounds that the codes are LOINC; the *item text* is the licensed part.

## Definition of done

- Licensing position confirmed under #64 (blocking).
- Channel chosen — see #337 for the three candidates and which are live.
- Offer made, with a link recorded here.
- `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md` §4.3 updated with the outcome.

## Notes

- Related: #337 (the other five build defects, and where to send them).
- Background: `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md` §4.3, and `ig/input/pagecontent/relationship-to-other-igs.md`, which already documents the eight-code match.

issues.title: "BHP bridge" demo: run the BH IG's own C-SSRS through SPiER's full pathway
issues.bodyMd:
Take the US Behavioral Health Profiles IG's **own** C-SSRS QuestionnaireResponse — their patient, their data, unmodified — and run it end to end through SPiER: fallback dispatch → tier Observation → risk episode → safety plan → follow-up → Stage-8 measure.

The argument it makes is the one SPiER most wants to make, and it makes it with someone else's artifact rather than our own.

## Why this is the highest-value demo available

Crosswalk row 54 of that IG maps "Suicide Risk Assessment" to *US Core QuestionnaireResponse + US Core Observation Screening Assessment* — and **ships only the QuestionnaireResponse half.** There is no suicide-risk Observation anywhere in the guide.

Their narrative makes the gap concrete without our help. In their seven-encounter story, James Wolff arrives at an ED, and the in-house psychiatrist "assessed a low risk for suicide based on the C-SSRS screen completed by the ED nurse." Then the story moves on. No derived concept, no safety plan, no follow-up contact, no risk episode, no measure. **The C-SSRS result is captured, coded, and dropped.**

That is the Capture → **Translate → Act** gap SPiER exists to fill, described in a federally funded IG, in the IG's own words, on the IG's own index patient. Given the SAMHSA/ASTP pilot cohort — 45 exchange partners across 9 states, testing complete end of 2026, resource published 2027 — a runnable demonstration that SPiER completes their story is plausibly the most persuasive artifact SPiER could build.

## Most of the machinery already exists

#325 landed the hard part: SPiER already reads their published C-SSRS and PHQ-9 examples verbatim, and recovers the same PHQ-9 total (12) and the same C-SSRS risk level the IG itself asserts. The fixtures are checked in at `web/src/lib/observationMappers/__fixtures__/` with provenance in the README there.

So the remaining work is a **scenario and a narration**, not new mapping logic.

## The one real design problem

**It needs a patient.** Their C-SSRS answers are all "No" → `none` tier, which derives no episode, no safety plan and no follow-up — so run literally, the demo shows nothing happening, which is the opposite of the point.

Options, roughly in order of honesty:

1. **Use their later encounter.** Their story escalates after the ED visit (PHQ-9 of 12, discontinued antidepressant, daily alcohol, a fall). Build the SPiER pathway from a *plausible subsequent* C-SSRS rather than the ED screen. Requires inventing an answer set — must be labelled as SPiER's extension of their scenario, never as their data.
2. **Show both arms**: their verbatim `none` result (correctly producing no episode — itself a useful demonstration that SPiER does not over-trigger), beside an endorsed variant that drives the full pathway. Most honest, and doubles as a specificity argument.
3. **A new demo patient** modelled on James Wolff.

⚠️ **Do not reuse `patient-011`.** That is Maria, and `docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.json` already tracks `branch-exclusive` walkthrough gaps that a different ED course cannot close on her. `patient-011.json` is also under concurrent edit by other sessions — see the warning in `docs/plans/next-session-handoff.md`.

**Option 2 is the recommendation**: it needs the least invention, and "SPiER correctly does nothing on a negative screen" is a claim worth being able to demonstrate to a federal audience.

## Attribution constraints

- Their example is CC0/HL7-published IG content, but the *scenario* is theirs. Any derived patient must be clearly SPiER's extension, in the same spirit as the `origin: "spier-proposed"` marker on the ED-scenario-11 steps.
- Do not present invented answers as the IG's data.
- The C-SSRS licensing question (#64) applies to anything that reproduces item text in a new demo surface.

## Definition of done

- A scenario (new patient or a documented variant) that runs their C-SSRS through the full pathway, with both arms if option 2.
- Walkthrough narration, so it is demonstrable rather than merely present in the data.
- `check:scenarios` and `validate-fhir.mjs` green on the new resources.
- The provenance boundary explicit in the scenario JSON and in whatever page presents it.

## Notes

- Background: `docs/research/2026-08-us-behavioral-health-profiles-ig.md` §2 and §4.2, and its item 9.
- Related: #337, #338 (upstream engagement); #326 gates the ED-scenario consent step but not this.
- This is the largest of the three BHP follow-ups and the only one that is a build rather than an outreach action.

issues.title: ED walkthrough narrates 21 artifacts the scenarios never materialize — and still calls TL-008 a profile gap
issues.bodyMd:
Found while fixing #324, and deliberately left out of that PR — it is a different class of problem and a much wider one.

## The finding

Across the four ED patients, **21 walkthrough steps narrated `status: completed` name a FHIR resource type SPiER profiles, but carry no `relatedRefs` to an artifact of that type**. A few examples:

| Patient | Step | Names | Has |
|---|---|---|---|
| patient-011 | 11.3-1D | `Observation`, `CareTeam` | — (1:1 continuous observation log) |
| patient-011 | 11.3-1B | `ServiceRequest` | — (suicide-precautions order) |
| patient-011 | 11.4-1B | `Observation`, `Condition`, `Flag` | — (risk level set + condition coded) |
| patient-011 | 11.6-2B | `Task`, `Flag` | — (discharge-readiness checklist) |
| patient-014 | 11.7-2C | `Flag` | Communication, Task only |

Most of these are defensible: a demo is not obliged to instantiate every artifact it describes, and several are genuinely aspirational (`List`, `CareTeam`, `Provenance` have no SPiER profile at all).

**But #324 proved the class can hide a real defect.** Patient-011's step 11.6-2A said "Lethal-means counseling delivered and documented", carried no Procedure, and the Stage-8 dashboard therefore scored her a *miss* on a step her own chart calls completed — for as long as the ED scenario had existed. That one is fixed, and `measures.narration.test.ts` now catches any repeat **where a measure scores the step**. The other 21 are unscored, so nothing looks at them.

## The related staleness

`docs/use-cases/ed-scenario-11.json` step 11.6-2A still reads:

```
"profileBinding": "**gap** — Lethal Means Counseling Procedure + Means-Safety Action profile (TL-008, status:planned, promote)",
"profileGaps": ["Lethal Means Counseling Procedure", "Means-Safety Action (who/what/when/where)"]
```

Both profiles exist (`ig/input/fsh/lethal-means.fsh`), TL-008 has a built recorder (`web/src/components/LethalMeansCounselingView.tsx`, #210), and two other patients carry conforming Procedures. So the workbook tells the HL7 working group SPiER has a gap it closed. The scenario walkthrough carried the same stale claim as `profileGap: true` — #324 fixed that copy, not the workbook's.

Worth a sweep: **how many of the workbook's other `**gap**` bindings describe tools that have since been built?** The gating-issue list would be the place to start, since each names a TL number whose status is checkable.

## Suggested shape

1. Re-check every `**gap**` binding in `ed-scenario-11.json` against the current profile set and tool statuses; a promotion means editing the JSON and rebuilding (`node scripts/build-use-case-workbook.mjs`), never the `dist/` outputs.
2. Decide per narrated step whether the artifact should be materialized in the scenario or the step should stop claiming the type. Both are fine answers; silently claiming it is not.
3. Consider extending the gate: for a step whose named type SPiER profiles AND whose tool is `built`, require a ref. Neither half alone is enough — I measured both and each produces ~21 findings today, which is why #324 did not take it on.

Refs #324, #52 (non-Questionnaire workflow artifacts), #210 (TL-008 recorder).
